Establish one central support player and two outside runners.
Use staggered starts for multiple groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball begins in an outside channel.
Players complete one short possession before switching the football towards the corridor.
The central support player accelerates into space and receives.
After disposing into the corridor, the original outside players run forward to support.
The group moves the football through the corridor and then releases to the opposite outside channel.
The final player kicks to the end target.
All players jog around the outside and reset at the starting end.
Complete continuous waves for two and a half minutes.
Walk for 60 seconds.
Repeat in the opposite direction for four total work periods.
coachingPoints: Maintain width before attacking the corridor.
Time the central run so the receiver arrives into space.
Kick to the receiver’s forward side.
Accelerate after the corridor entry.
Continue running to support the next disposal.
Avoid all players collapsing into the central lane.
Use controlled recovery around the outside.
Preserve field shape throughout each wave.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether outside players maintain width.
Whether the corridor runner moves at the correct time.
Whether the group accelerates after entering the corridor.
Whether support runners remain available forward of possession.
Whether fatigue causes the group to lose its shape.

commonErrors.error: Players enter the corridor too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside positions until the first switch is completed.

commonErrors.error: Central receiver waits stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the run as the outside kicker prepares to dispose.

commonErrors.error: All runners follow the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one corridor, one inside-support and one outside-support lane.

commonErrors.error: Final kick is attempted without balance.
commonErrors.correction: Require the final player to control speed before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Recovery becomes a race back to the start.
commonErrors.correction: Use the outside return as controlled active recovery.

progressions: Add one passive defender in the corridor.
Require the group to make a live decision between corridor and outside use.
Reduce the width of the central corridor.
Add a turnover consequence if the final target is missed.
Increase wave duration to three minutes.
regressions: Reduce the work period to 90 seconds.
matchApplication: Teams frequently move the football from the boundary side into the corridor to create faster forward movement. This drill develops the running work required to shift field position and continue supporting after the switch.

title: Defensive Recovery to Outlet
primarySkill: Defensive recovery running followed by attacking outlet movement
objective: Develop the ability to recover defensively at speed, regain structure and then transition into an attacking outlet when possession is won.
groundSize: A 55-metre by 40-metre area divided into defensive, contest and outlet zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a defensive starting line at one end.
Create a contest zone 25 metres away.
Place two outlet gates on each side of the area.
Organise groups of five to seven.
Position one feeder beyond the contest zone.
Allocate two defenders, two support players and one outlet runner.
Use controlled pressure only in the contest zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The group begins moving forward away from the defensive starting line.
On the coach’s turnover call, all players turn and recover towards the contest zone.
The feeder sends a rolling or bouncing football into the zone.
The first defender secures or knocks the football to a supporting teammate.
Once possession is controlled, the group transitions towards either outlet gate.
The outside runner accelerates to receive a handball or short kick.
The group completes the outlet and continues through the gate.
Players walk back to the starting position.
Complete five to eight repetitions.
Alternate the side of the outlet and starting roles.
coachingPoints: React immediately to the turnover call.
Recover towards goal-side positions.
Communicate defensive roles while running.
Slow under control when entering the contest zone.
Secure possession before attempting the outlet.
Spread quickly once the football is won.
Accelerate to the outside outlet.
Use the walk-back as recovery.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players react immediately to the turnover cue.
Whether recovery lines protect the central area.
Whether players remain balanced entering the contest.
Whether outside runners spread after possession is secured.
Whether the outlet disposal is accurate under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players jog slowly after the turnover call.
commonErrors.correction: Demand a decisive first five metres of recovery.

commonErrors.error: All players chase the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one contest player, one cover player and outside support roles.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt to attack before securing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Require a clean possession or controlled release before spreading.

commonErrors.error: Outlet runner leaves too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold defensive shape until possession is clearly won.

commonErrors.error: Central space remains unprotected.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through the corridor before widening.

progressions: Add an active opponent in the contest zone.
Allow the coach to choose either outlet gate late.
Add a second attacking disposal after the outlet.
Reduce recovery between repetitions.
Begin players from different field positions.
successIndicators: Spread immediately after winning the football.
matchApplication: After losing possession, players must recover defensively. When the football is regained, they must rapidly change mindset and provide an outlet. This drill conditions both phases within one repeated effort.

title: Repeat Lead and Fold
primarySkill: Repeated leading followed by defensive folding movement
objective: Develop the ability to lead strongly for possession and immediately fold back into a defensive support position after disposal.
groundSize: Four to six channels measuring 45 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Place a feeder at one end of each channel.
Mark a lead cone 15 metres forward and a fold cone 12 metres behind the feeder.
Position a target player 15 metres beyond the lead cone.
Organise three or four players per channel.
Establish three working repetitions before role rotation.
Allow 45 seconds recovery between sequences.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working player begins beside the feeder.
On the feeder’s signal, the player accelerates to the lead cone.
The feeder kicks to the leading player.
The player marks and kicks to the forward target.
Immediately after disposing, the player turns and folds back past the feeder to the defensive cone.
The player receives a handball from the feeder at the defensive cone.
The player returns the handball and begins the next lead.
Complete three lead-and-fold repetitions.
Rotate the worker, feeder and target.
Complete three or four sequences per player.
coachingPoints: Lead with full commitment.
Present a clear target for the kick.
Control momentum before marking.
Dispose accurately before beginning the fold.
Turn immediately after the kick.
Recover through a direct inside line.
Communicate during the defensive fold.
Repeat the same movement quality across all three efforts.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the third lead matches the first.
Whether the player turns immediately after disposal.
Whether the fold line is direct and purposeful.
Whether marking and kicking remain clean.
Whether recovery between sequences is sufficient.

commonErrors.error: Player admires the kick before recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Make the turn compulsory immediately after contact.

commonErrors.error: Defensive fold drifts too wide.
commonErrors.correction: Use a central fold cone and direct recovery line.

commonErrors.error: Player arrives at the lead cone out of control.
commonErrors.correction: Begin decelerating before the marking point.

commonErrors.error: Later leads lose intensity.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the sequence to two repetitions or increase recovery.

commonErrors.error: Feeder delivers before the lead is established.
commonErrors.correction: Release the kick only when the player creates separation.

progressions: Add a passive defender on the lead.
Require the target to handball back into the recovering player’s path.
Increase the fold distance.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Add a live decision between two lead cones.
successIndicators: Recover through the correct defensive line.
Repeat the full sequence with consistent intent.
matchApplication: Players must often transition from attacking involvement to defensive responsibility within seconds. This drill conditions the habit of folding back immediately after a lead and disposal.

title: Transition Run-and-Kick Relay
primarySkill: Repeated transition running with kicking execution
objective: Develop repeated transition running while requiring players to execute accurate kicks before handing the next effort to a teammate.
groundSize: Four to six lanes measuring 50 metres by 10 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a start line, central kicking line and end target gate.
Position half the players at each end of the lane.
Place one football with the first player.
Mark a five-metre handover zone at both ends.
Ensure lanes are separated.
Use team groups of four to six.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player accelerates from the start line while carrying the football.
At the central line, the player kicks through the target gate to the first player at the far end.
The kicker continues running into the far handover zone.
The receiver marks or gathers the football and immediately begins the return effort.
The outgoing and incoming players communicate and avoid crossing paths.
Continue for 90 seconds.
Walk for 60 seconds.
Complete four rounds.
Change the kicking foot or kick type between rounds.
Award one point for every accurate kick completed without breaking the relay rhythm.
coachingPoints: Accelerate strongly from the handover zone.
Carry the football securely.
Control speed before kicking.
Kick through the target rather than simply towards it.
Continue running after disposal.
Communicate with the next runner.
Use the recovery period actively.
Maintain consistent effort across the full relay.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player remains balanced before kicking.
Whether running continues after disposal.
Whether the next player begins at the correct time.
Whether fatigue affects target accuracy.
Whether handovers remain safe and organised.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks at full speed without balance.
commonErrors.correction: Use two control steps before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Kicker stops after releasing the football.
commonErrors.correction: Require the kicker to run through the handover zone.

commonErrors.error: Next runner leaves before controlling the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the mark or gather before accelerating.

commonErrors.error: Players collide in the handover zone.
commonErrors.correction: Assign separate entry and exit sides.

commonErrors.error: Relay pace is too fast to sustain accuracy.
commonErrors.correction: Set a repeatable running target rather than maximal speed.

progressions: Reduce recovery between rounds.
Add a bounce before the kick.
Use a moving target instead of a gate.
Add a passive defender near the kicking line.
Require alternate-foot kicking.
regressions: Use handball through the target gate.
Increase the width of the target.
successIndicators: Maintain relay rhythm across repeated rounds.
matchApplication: Transition passages require players to run hard, execute a kick and continue supporting the next phase. This drill combines those actions in a repeated team conditioning format.

title: Boundary-to-Boundary Winger Endurance
objective: Develop the ability to repeatedly provide width, receive along the outside channel and recover into the next supporting position.
groundSize: Two outside channels, each 70 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark two long channels near each boundary side.
Place stations at 0, 25, 50 and 70 metres.
Position players evenly at each station.
Use one football per channel.
Establish a forward wave and a recovery line outside the channel.
Allocate players to left and right sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first player leads from the 25-metre station and receives a kick from the start.
After marking, the player turns and kicks to the player leading from the 50-metre station.
The possession continues to the 70-metre station.
Each player follows the kick for five to ten metres before exiting into the outside recovery line.
Players jog back along the recovery line to the station behind them.
The wave restarts from the opposite end.
Continue for three minutes.
Walk for 60 seconds.
Complete four work periods.
Swap players between left and right channels halfway through.
coachingPoints: Hold width within the outside channel.
Lead early and at an angle.
Kick to the receiver’s forward side.
Follow the disposal briefly before recovering.
Use the outside return line to avoid congestion.
Maintain an even work rate.
Communicate down the channel.
Preserve kicking quality late in each period.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain wide positioning.
Whether leads begin early enough.
Whether kicks allow forward movement.
Whether recovery paths remain outside the possession channel.
Whether players can repeat the running workload.

commonErrors.error: Players drift towards the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Use boundary cones and require possession within the wide channel.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the lead before the kicker settles.

commonErrors.error: Kick is placed behind the lead.
commonErrors.correction: Aim to the receiver’s forward shoulder.

commonErrors.error: Recovery runners cut through the active channel.
commonErrors.correction: Use a separate outside recovery lane.

commonErrors.error: Later waves lose width.
commonErrors.correction: Reset station positions during recovery.

progressions: Add a passive defender to each receiving station.
Require one kick to travel 30–35 metres.
Reduce the recovery period.
Add a switch from one channel to the other.
Use a live decision to continue wide or attack inside.
successIndicators: Recover through the correct outside line.
Repeat the work across all periods.
matchApplication: Wingers and outside players cover large distances while holding width, presenting as kick options and recovering into the next phase. This drill develops those repeated wide-running demands.

title: Inside-Outside Support Circuit
primarySkill: Alternating inside and outside support running
objective: Develop the ability to alternate between close inside support and wider outside support while maintaining continuous movement.
groundSize: Three to four circuits measuring approximately 30 metres by 25 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark an inner diamond with four cones.
Mark a larger outside square around the diamond.
Organise three to six players per circuit.
Place one player at each starting position.
Use one football.
Designate inside cones for handball support and outside cones for kicking support.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins on an outside cone.
The player handballs to a teammate leading to an inside cone.
After disposing, the original player runs to the next outside cone.
The inside receiver turns and kicks to the outside support player.
The kicker then moves to the next inside cone.
Players continue alternating between inside and outside roles.
Complete two minutes of continuous movement.
Walk for 40 seconds.
Reverse the direction.
Complete four to five work periods.
coachingPoints: Accelerate into the inside support position.
Maintain width when moving to the outside.
Use handball for close support and kick for wider support.
Move immediately after disposal.
Scan before entering the inside space.
Avoid two players occupying the same support cone.
Communicate the next option.
Maintain controlled pace throughout the circuit.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the alternating movement pattern.
Whether inside support arrives at the correct time.
Whether outside support maintains width.
Whether players scan before changing roles.
Whether fatigue causes spacing errors.

commonErrors.error: Players remain on the same movement line.
commonErrors.correction: Require every player to alternate between an inner and outer cone.

commonErrors.error: Inside support arrives too early.
commonErrors.correction: Delay the run until the ball carrier controls possession.

commonErrors.error: Outside players drift inward.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the outer square as the required receiving area.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Make the next support movement immediate.

commonErrors.error: Circuit becomes confusing after an error.
commonErrors.correction: Reset at the nearest open cone and restart the direction.

progressions: Add one passive defender inside the diamond.
Allow the ball carrier to choose either inside option.
Add a second football.
Reduce the outside square size.
Require non-preferred-side disposal.
regressions: Remove one side of the circuit.
successIndicators: Alternate between inside and outside support.
Sustain the pattern throughout the work period.
matchApplication: Effective ball movement requires close support near possession and wider options outside pressure. This drill develops the conditioning and awareness required to move repeatedly between both roles.

title: Fatigue Decision Running Box
primarySkill: Running decision making under controlled fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select and execute the correct football option after completing a repeated movement effort.
groundSize: Four to six grids measuring 20 metres by 20 metres.
equipment: Four coloured target gates per grid
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place a start cone in the centre of each grid.
Position four differently coloured target gates around the outside.
Place one feeder beside the centre.
Organise two to four working players per grid.
Mark four short running cones around the central start.
Set a 20-second movement effort followed by one disposal decision.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working player begins at the central cone.
On the whistle, the player completes four short movements to nominated running cones.
The player returns to the centre after each movement.
During the final return, the feeder delivers a handball.
At the moment of release, the coach calls one target colour.
The player receives, turns and disposes through the nominated gate.
The player retrieves the football at walking pace.
Rotate the worker and feeder.
Complete four to six repetitions each.
Vary the running pattern and disposal type between rounds.
coachingPoints: Maintain safe footwork during the movement effort.
Keep the head up when returning to the centre.
Regain balance before receiving.
Identify the target before beginning the disposal action.
Use the correct disposal for distance and angle.
Avoid guessing the target.
Complete recovery at walking pace.
Reduce movement volume if decision quality collapses.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain movement control.
Whether they scan before receiving.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether fatigue causes rushed technique.
Whether decision speed remains stable across repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Player guesses the target before the call.
commonErrors.correction: Vary the timing and require visual confirmation.

commonErrors.error: Player receives while off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Return to a stable central position before taking possession.

commonErrors.error: Disposal choice does not suit the target distance.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce handball for close gates and kick for longer gates.

commonErrors.error: Movement effort is too intense for accurate decision making.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the number of running cones.

commonErrors.error: Player looks down after receiving.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate target identification before moving the football.

progressions: Add one passive defender.
Use two target calls with one becoming unavailable.
Increase running effort to 25 seconds.
Add a ground-ball receive.
Require the player to choose the most appropriate open target.
successIndicators: Maintain decision quality across repeated efforts.
matchApplication: Players are often required to make important decisions after running, chasing or changing direction. This drill develops the ability to regain composure and select an effective option under controlled fatigue.
relatedDrills: CF-008 – Clean Skills Under Light Fatigue

title: Movement Conditioning Block Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated assessment of football movement conditioning
objective: Assess whether players can apply the movement-conditioning principles developed in CF-021 to CF-029 within an integrated football activity.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval divided into five assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Create five connected zones:
Pace Zone: Controlled running followed by acceleration.
Overlap Zone: Give-and-go handball support.
Width Zone: Outside possession into corridor support.
Recovery Zone: Defensive fold followed by outlet movement.
Decision Zone: Target selection after a movement effort.
Divide players into groups of three to six.
Start each group at a different zone.
Allocate three minutes per zone.
Allow 45 seconds to rotate.
Prepare assessment categories covering movement timing, positioning, repeatability, skill execution and decision quality.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete the Change-of-Pace Zone using the required running-speed sequence.
In the Overlap Zone, players handball, accelerate and receive again.
In the Width Zone, players hold an outside position before supporting into the corridor.
In the Recovery Zone, players fold defensively and then transition to an outlet.
In the Decision Zone, players complete a movement effort before selecting a target.
Coaches observe and record specific behaviours at each zone.
Groups rotate after three minutes.
Complete all five zones.
Allow three minutes of active recovery.
Repeat any zone requiring additional observation.
Finish with individual or group feedback.
coachingPoints: Assess movement purpose rather than total running alone.
Observe whether players change pace appropriately.
Reward immediate movement after disposal.
Assess whether players maintain width and support spacing.
Monitor defensive recovery and attacking transition.
Record skill quality under fatigue.
Assess decision making after repeated movement.
Modify standards for age, position and return-to-play status.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players use different running speeds effectively.
Whether overlap timing is correct.
Whether players maintain width before moving inside.
Whether defensive recovery lines protect central space.
Whether decisions remain accurate under fatigue.
Whether skill execution remains controlled.
Whether players repeat movement efforts consistently.
Whether recovery habits support the next task.

commonErrors.error: Players treat every zone as a sprint test.
commonErrors.correction: Re-explain the movement objective and required intensity of each zone.

commonErrors.error: Coaches record only running speed.
commonErrors.correction: Assess positioning, skill, timing and decisions as separate categories.

commonErrors.error: Players lose shape as fatigue builds.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration or increase rotation recovery.

commonErrors.error: Movement patterns are completed without football purpose.
commonErrors.correction: Require each movement to create, support or defend a possession option.

commonErrors.error: Results are compared without accounting for player role.
commonErrors.correction: Use positional and individual benchmarks.

commonErrors.error: Players stop completely between zones.
commonErrors.correction: Require walking recovery and early organisation at the next station.

progressions: Add controlled opposition at selected zones.
Reduce rotation recovery.
Add position-specific assessment standards.
Record accuracy and repeat-effort consistency.
Repeat the assessment after a targeted training block.
successIndicators: Change pace at the correct moments.
Support from useful inside and outside positions.
Make accurate decisions after movement efforts.
matchApplication: The assessment integrates the running patterns required in Australian football: changing pace, overlapping, holding width, supporting through the corridor, recovering defensively and making decisions after repeated movement.

title: Inside-Midfield Repeat Exit
objective: Develop the ability to win or receive the football in a congested area, accelerate into space, release cleanly and recover for another involvement.
groundSize: Three to four grids measuring 25 metres by 20 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a six-metre central congestion square.
Place four exit gates around the outside of the grid.
Organise groups of three: one working midfielder, one feeder and one support player.
Position the feeder outside the congestion square.
Position the support player beyond one exit gate.
Begin with controlled pressure only.
Use 30-second work periods with 50 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working midfielder begins inside the congestion square.
The feeder rolls or handballs the football into the square.
The midfielder collects or receives and immediately scans for the nominated exit gate.
The player accelerates from the congestion square and handballs to the support player.
The midfielder continues past the support player to receive a return handball.
The midfielder disposes back to the feeder.
The player returns to the central square and repeats the sequence.
Complete as many clean repetitions as possible in 30 seconds.
Rotate roles during the 50-second recovery.
Complete four to six work periods.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with the body balanced and low.
Protect the football before attempting to exit.
Scan while collecting rather than after possession is secured.
Use the first two steps to accelerate clear of congestion.
Handball to the support player’s forward side.
Continue past the support player rather than stopping after disposal.
Recover quickly to the central square.
Maintain clean execution rather than chasing excessive repetition numbers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players secure possession before accelerating.
Whether the correct exit gate is identified.
Whether the first steps create separation.
Whether the return handball is received at speed.
Whether repeated efforts remain technically controlled.

commonErrors.error: Player remains upright when collecting.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and keep the body behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Player pauses before selecting an exit.
commonErrors.correction: Require scanning as the football approaches.

commonErrors.error: Handball is delivered behind the support runner.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the forward hand.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after first disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Make the receive-back movement compulsory.

commonErrors.error: Later repetitions become rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work time or increase recovery.

progressions: Add a passive defender in the congestion square.
Allow the coach to change the exit gate late.
Require a short kick after the return handball.
Reduce recovery to 35–40 seconds.
Add a second support player and live exit choice.
successIndicators: Maintain skill quality across the set.
matchApplication: Inside midfielders repeatedly win or receive the football in congestion, accelerate into space, release to support and then remain involved in the next possession. This drill develops that repeated movement pattern.

title: Forward-Half Pressure-to-Spread Runs
primarySkill: Repeated pressure effort followed by attacking spread
objective: Develop the ability to apply a high-intensity forward-half pressure effort and immediately spread into attacking space when possession is regained.
groundSize: A 45-metre by 40-metre forward-half area.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central possession zone 20 metres from goal.
Place two scoring gates in each forward pocket area.
Organise one attacking group of four and one defending group of two or three.
Position a feeder outside the area.
Allocate one resting group that rotates in after each repetition.
Use 20–25-second repetitions with 40–50 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder begins with possession and passes to a defender.
The attacking group applies coordinated pressure for six to eight seconds.
On the coach’s turnover call, the feeder sends a loose football into the central zone.
The attacking players change from pressure to attacking spread.
One player secures the football while teammates lead towards separate scoring gates.
The group must complete a disposal through one gate.
All players recover to their starting positions.
Rotate attackers, defenders and resting players.
Complete six to ten repetitions.
Award one point for a forced error and one point for a clean scoring disposal after the turnover.
coachingPoints: Accelerate immediately when applying pressure.
Approach under control rather than overrunning the ball carrier.
Communicate which player pressures and which players cover exits.
Change mindset immediately when possession becomes available.
Spread to different lanes after the turnover.
Avoid all players running towards the football.
Execute the final disposal under control.
Use the recovery period to reset roles.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether pressure efforts are coordinated.
Whether players react immediately to the turnover.
Whether attacking spread creates multiple options.
Whether players recover their breathing and roles before the next repetition.
Whether skill execution remains clean after the pressure effort.

commonErrors.error: All attackers chase the same opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one pressure player and supporting cover roles.

commonErrors.error: Players overrun the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate with short steps before applying pressure.

commonErrors.error: Attackers remain clustered after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Require separate lead lanes to different gates.

commonErrors.error: Final disposal is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and take a balanced step before release.

commonErrors.error: Repetitions restart before players are organised.
commonErrors.correction: Use the final 10 seconds of recovery to reset positions.

progressions: Add another defender.
Allow the turnover to occur without a coach call.
Require a kick rather than handball through the gate.
Reduce recovery time.
Add a second possession after the first score.
regressions: Reduce the pressure period to four seconds.
successIndicators: Repeat pressure efforts with consistent intent.
matchApplication: Forward-half players must often chase, pressure and then immediately attack after a turnover. This drill conditions the rapid change from defensive effort to attacking movement.

title: Half-Back Rebound Running Waves
objective: Develop the ability to win or receive possession in defence, accelerate into rebound support and recover into defensive structure after the attacking wave.
groundSize: A 70-metre by 50-metre area beginning inside defensive 50.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark an intercept zone inside defensive 50.
Place two outlet gates near half-back.
Place two continuation targets near the end of the area.
Organise groups of five or six.
Assign one interceptor, two support runners, one outside runner and one final target.
Start each wave from a coach or feeder kick into the intercept zone.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks or rolls the football into the intercept zone.
The interceptor secures the football and releases by handball or short kick.
The first support runner accelerates past possession.
The group moves the football through one outlet gate.
The outside runner continues to receive and kick to the final target.
After the final kick, all players recover towards the original defensive positions.
Players must be reset before the next wave starts.
Complete one wave every 35–45 seconds.
Rotate roles after two waves.
Complete eight to twelve waves.
coachingPoints: Secure the intercept before attempting rebound.
Spread immediately once possession is controlled.
Use the first support runner to create forward momentum.
Maintain an outside option.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Continue running after disposal.
Recover through the corridor after the wave.
Re-establish defensive positions before the next repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the intercept is controlled cleanly.
Whether support runners accelerate at the correct time.
Whether rebound shape includes inside and outside options.
Whether players recover immediately after the final disposal.
Whether repeated waves retain structure and accuracy.

commonErrors.error: Players spread before possession is secured.
commonErrors.correction: Hold shape until the intercept is clearly controlled.

commonErrors.error: Support runners remain behind the football.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate past possession after the first release.

commonErrors.error: All players use the same running lane.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate inside, outside and overlap roles.

commonErrors.error: Players walk back after the wave.
commonErrors.correction: Require controlled recovery running to defensive positions.

commonErrors.error: Final kick becomes inaccurate under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce wave frequency or increase recovery.

progressions: Add a passive forward applying pressure to the interceptor.
Allow the group to choose between two outlet gates.
Add a turnover consequence.
Increase the wave distance.
Reduce the time available to reset.
regressions: Use handball only for the first two possessions.
successIndicators: Recover to defensive structure before the next wave.
matchApplication: Half-backs repeatedly intercept, rebound, overlap and then recover when the attacking phase ends. This drill conditions the running and skill demands of that complete movement cycle.

title: Ruck-to-Contest Repeat Efforts
objective: Develop the ability to complete a ruck contest, follow up at ground level and reposition for repeated stoppage involvements.
groundSize: Two to four stoppage grids measuring 20 metres by 20 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central ruck circle in each grid.
Place two exit gates on opposite sides.
Organise one ruck, one opposition ruck or bag holder, two midfielders and one feeder.
Establish clear legal-contact rules.
Use four-contest sequences with 60–75 seconds recovery.
Adjust jump and bodywork demands for age and training status.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder throws or bounces the football into the ruck contest.
The ruck competes or works against controlled resistance.
Immediately after the hit-out, the ruck follows the football to ground level.
The ruck applies pressure, blocks or receives a handball from a midfielder.
The group exits through one nominated gate.
All players reset quickly for the next stoppage.
Complete four stoppage efforts in the sequence.
Walk and recover for 60–75 seconds.
Rotate rucks and midfield roles.
Complete three or four sequences.
coachingPoints: Use safe and legal ruck technique.
Land with balance after jumping.
Locate the football immediately after the hit-out.
Accelerate into the follow-up contest.
Avoid standing and watching the midfielders.
Use body positioning to create space legally.
Reset promptly for the next stoppage.
Reduce jump volume if landing quality declines.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the ruck lands safely.
Whether follow-up movement begins immediately.
Whether second efforts are useful rather than uncontrolled.
Whether legal bodywork creates space.
Whether repeated contests remain technically safe.

commonErrors.error: Ruck watches the hit-out after landing.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate movement towards the contest.

commonErrors.error: Landing is stiff or off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce jump height and coach soft, balanced landing.

commonErrors.error: Follow-up contact is reckless.
commonErrors.correction: Use controlled body positioning and clear legal-contact limits.

commonErrors.error: Reset becomes slow after each stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate exact starting positions and a reset time.

commonErrors.error: Jump quality declines sharply.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the number of contests per sequence.

progressions: Add live midfield opposition.
Use different stoppage types.
Require the ruck to become the outlet player.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Add a repeat contest after the initial clearance.
regressions: Use a ruck bag rather than an opponent.
Remove jumping and use boundary throw-in positioning.
successIndicators: Maintain technical quality across the sequence.
matchApplication: Rucks must repeatedly contest, land, follow up, block, tackle and support clearances. This drill conditions the complete stoppage effort rather than treating the hit-out as an isolated action.

title: Key-Position Lead-and-Recover Circuit
objective: Develop the ability of key-position players to complete repeated leads, marking actions and recovery movements while preserving movement and skill quality.
groundSize: Two to four channels measuring 45 metres by 15 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Place a feeder at one end of each channel.
Mark three lead cones: straight, angled and double-back.
Position a recovery cone behind the starting point.
Place a target player beyond the lead area.
Organise groups of three or four.
Set three-lead sequences with 60 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working player begins near the feeder.
The player completes a straight lead and receives a kick.
After marking, the player kicks to the target.
The player recovers around the rear cone.
The feeder directs the second angled lead.
The player completes the mark, disposal and recovery.
The third effort uses a double-back or change-of-direction lead.
After the third disposal, the player walks through recovery.
Rotate worker, feeder and target roles.
Complete three or four sequences each.
coachingPoints: Use powerful first steps into each lead.
Create separation before calling for the football.
Control speed before marking.
Present strong hands.
Kick accurately after the mark.
Recover immediately after disposal.
Maintain running posture despite fatigue.
Adjust repetition volume for larger players and return-to-play athletes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether lead speed is maintained.
Whether the player controls momentum before marking.
Whether the third lead remains technically sound.
Whether recovery begins immediately.
Whether kick accuracy changes through the sequence.

commonErrors.error: Player begins every lead from the same angle.
commonErrors.correction: Use clearly separated lead cones.

commonErrors.error: Player arrives too fast to mark cleanly.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate over the final two or three steps.

commonErrors.error: Recovery becomes a walk after the first effort.
commonErrors.correction: Require controlled running to the rear cone.

commonErrors.error: Third disposal becomes rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery between leads or reduce sequence length.

commonErrors.error: Player calls before creating separation.
commonErrors.correction: Lead first, then communicate when the lane is open.

progressions: Add controlled body pressure.
Allow the feeder to choose the lead late.
Add a contested mark on one repetition.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Extend the final disposal distance.
matchApplication: Key-position players perform repeated powerful efforts rather than constant running. This drill develops the capacity to lead, mark, dispose and recover before presenting again.

title: Small-Forward Crumb-and-Chase Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to react to a dropped or spoiled football, accelerate to the crumb, finish or release, and immediately apply a second pressure effort.
groundSize: Two to four forward-pocket grids measuring 25 metres by 20 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a starting cone 15 metres from goal.
Position a feeder near the boundary side.
Place a chasing cone five metres behind the worker.
Organise one working forward, one feeder, one chaser and one retriever.
Use 20-second work periods with 50 seconds recovery.
Begin with controlled shadow pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working forward starts in front of the chaser.
The feeder sends a bouncing or rolling football into the scoring area.
The forward accelerates to collect the crumb.
The forward attempts a snap, handball through a gate or short kick to a target.
Immediately after disposal, the feeder releases a second football towards the opposite side.
The forward and chaser compete to reach the second football.
The forward either regains possession or applies pressure.
Complete two connected efforts per repetition.
Rotate roles.
Complete four to six repetitions each.
coachingPoints: React immediately to the football’s movement.
Approach the crumb under control.
Keep the body between the opponent and football.
Finish quickly but remain balanced.
Transition immediately into the second effort.
Chase with intent even after missing the first possession.
Use legal pressure only.
Maintain effort quality across repetitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the forward reads the football early.
Whether collection technique remains clean.
Whether the first disposal is controlled.
Whether the second effort begins immediately.
Whether chasing remains legal and purposeful.

commonErrors.error: Forward guesses where the football will land.
commonErrors.correction: Track the ball flight and adjust late.

commonErrors.error: Player overruns the crumb.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and lower the hips.

commonErrors.error: First shot is rushed off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and establish a stable base.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after the first disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Release the second football immediately to demand reaction.

commonErrors.error: Chaser makes unsafe contact.
commonErrors.correction: Use shadow pressure and clear no-push rules.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure.
Vary the second football’s direction.
Require a non-preferred-side finish.
Reduce recovery.
Add a third repeat pressure effort.
successIndicators: React immediately to the second effort.
Apply useful pressure when possession is lost.
matchApplication: Small forwards repeatedly crumb, finish, chase and pressure within short passages. This drill conditions the quick successive efforts required around goal.

title: Wing Switch and Reposition Run
primarySkill: Repeated repositioning after a switch of play
objective: Develop the ability to hold width, react to a switch of play and reposition rapidly to support the next phase.
groundSize: A 70-metre by 60-metre area with two outside channels.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark left and right wing channels.
Place two central switch stations.
Position players at each wing and central station.
Begin with the football in one wing channel.
Nominate one wide player as the primary repositioning runner.
Create a return lane behind play for recovery movement.
howTheDrillWorks:
The football begins in one wing channel.
Players complete a short possession before kicking into a central switch station.
The opposite winger holds width and begins a timed acceleration.
The central player switches the football to the opposite wing.
The winger marks and kicks forward to a target.
After disposal, the original winger runs behind play to reposition on the new attacking side.
Players rotate through the wing, central and target roles.
Complete continuous waves for three minutes.
Walk for 60 seconds.
Repeat for four work periods.
coachingPoints: Hold width until the switch becomes available.
Begin the repositioning run before the central player disposes.
Accelerate into the receiving space.
Kick to the winger’s forward side.
Continue running after the wing possession.
Use the recovery lane behind play.
Scan the football and teammates while repositioning.
Maintain spacing as fatigue increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the far-side winger maintains width.
Whether the acceleration is timed correctly.
Whether the switch kick allows forward movement.
Whether players reposition after disposal.
Whether the structure remains balanced across repeated waves.

commonErrors.error: Far-side winger moves inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the outside channel until the switch is initiated.

commonErrors.error: Winger waits flat-footed for the kick.
commonErrors.correction: Begin the run as the central player receives.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick is too high or behind.
commonErrors.correction: Kick to space in front of the winger.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the final kick.
commonErrors.correction: Use the designated recovery and repositioning lane.

commonErrors.error: Both wings collapse to the same side.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one player in each outside channel at all times.

progressions: Add a passive defender in each wing channel.
Allow the central player to choose whether to switch.
Add a return switch.
Reduce recovery between work periods.
Require a longer final kick.
matchApplication: Wing players must repeatedly hold width, react to switches, support forward movement and reposition when the football changes sides. This drill develops those repeated outside-running demands.

title: Interchange Re-entry Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to recover briefly, identify the match situation and re-enter play at the required intensity and position.
groundSize: A 50-metre by 45-metre playing area with an interchange box.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a small interchange box outside the playing area.
Place four entry gates representing defensive, midfield, wing and forward roles.
Organise a continuous possession activity inside the playing area.
Keep two to four players rotating through the interchange box.
Assign each resting player a likely re-entry role.
Use 30–45-second recovery periods.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players inside the area maintain possession under controlled pressure.
A coach calls one player to the interchange box.
The player exits, walks and controls breathing for 30–45 seconds.
During recovery, the player must watch the game and identify team shape.
The coach calls a role or coloured entry gate.
The player re-enters through the correct gate at the required intensity.
The player must immediately provide a possession or defensive option.
Another player rotates off.
Continue for four- to five-minute blocks.
Complete three or four blocks with two minutes recovery between blocks.
coachingPoints: Begin recovery immediately after leaving the field.
Remain mentally connected while recovering.
Scan team shape before re-entry.
Enter through the correct positional gate.
Accelerate into a useful role rather than simply running fast.
Communicate before crossing into the playing area.
Use the first involvement cleanly.
Adjust recovery duration for individual workload needs.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players remain engaged during recovery.
Whether they recognise the correct entry gate.
Whether re-entry movement improves team structure.
Whether the first football action is controlled.
Whether recovery duration supports quality re-entry.

commonErrors.error: Player switches off during recovery.
commonErrors.correction: Require the player to identify the current game shape before re-entry.

commonErrors.error: Player enters through the wrong gate.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the role verbally before releasing the player.

commonErrors.error: Player sprints into a crowded area.
commonErrors.correction: Scan and choose a useful entry line.

commonErrors.error: First disposal is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Balance and assess options before releasing the football.

commonErrors.error: Recovery is identical for all players.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust time according to load, age and role.

progressions: Change the re-entry role late.
Add scoreboard or time scenarios.
Reduce recovery duration.
Require the re-entering player to make the first defensive or attacking action.
Track successful first involvements.
matchApplication: Interchange players must recover physically without disconnecting mentally. On re-entry, they need to understand the match situation and immediately contribute to team structure.
relatedDrills: CF-037 – Wing Switch and Reposition Run

title: Continuous Three-Phase Transition Game
primarySkill: Repeated movement across attack, defence and recovery phases
objective: Develop the ability to repeatedly move through attacking, defensive and recovery phases while maintaining team structure and football skill.
groundSize: A 70-metre by 55-metre area divided into three horizontal zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the area into defensive, midfield and attacking zones.
Organise two even teams.
Place two scoring gates at each end.
Nominate a recovery channel along one boundary.
Use four-minute playing blocks.
Begin with one football and controlled opposition.
Allow free player movement between zones after disposal.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in attack and attempts to score through an end gate.
After a score or turnover, possession immediately changes direction.
The former attacking team must recover defensively.
The new attacking team spreads and moves through the midfield zone.
After two consecutive high-intensity transitions, the coach calls a recovery phase.
During recovery, possession continues at controlled tempo in the midfield zone.
After 20 seconds, the coach calls live play and both teams accelerate into the next phase.
Continue for four minutes.
Walk and review for 90 seconds.
Complete four to five blocks.
coachingPoints: Recognise the current phase immediately.
Accelerate during the first moments of transition.
Recover through central defensive lanes.
Spread after possession is won.
Use controlled movement during the recovery phase.
Maintain communication through all phases.
Preserve disposal quality under fatigue.
Avoid unnecessary maximal running when the game is in a low-intensity phase.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify the phase quickly.
Whether transition efforts are decisive.
Whether defensive recovery protects central space.
Whether attacking spread creates width.
Whether recovery phases are used efficiently.
Whether skill and decision quality survive repeated transitions.

commonErrors.error: Players continue attacking after possession is lost.
commonErrors.correction: Use an immediate turnover call and require defensive recovery.

commonErrors.error: All defenders chase the football.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through assigned central and outside lanes.

commonErrors.error: Players sprint during the recovery phase.
commonErrors.correction: Set clear controlled-tempo rules.

commonErrors.error: Attacking team remains narrow.
commonErrors.correction: Award bonus points for using both outside lanes.

commonErrors.error: Skill quality collapses late in the block.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce block length or increase recovery.

progressions: Add a second football.
Remove coach-controlled recovery phases.
Increase defensive pressure.
Add scoreboard scenarios.
Extend blocks to five minutes.
successIndicators: Use lower-intensity phases for active recovery.
Maintain football skill across repeated transitions.
matchApplication: Australian football alternates continuously between attacking, defending, transitioning and recovering. This game conditions players to manage all phases rather than treating running efforts in isolation.

title: Movement Application Assessment
objective: Assess whether players can apply the movement and positional conditioning behaviours developed through CF-031 to CF-039 within repeated football scenarios.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval divided into five positional assessment stations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create five assessment stations:
Midfield Exit: Ground-ball win and acceleration from congestion.
Forward Pressure: Pressure effort followed by attacking spread.
Defensive Rebound: Intercept, overlap and recovery.
Position-Specific Repeat Effort: Ruck, key-position or small-forward movement.
Three-Phase Game: Attack, defence and recovery transition.
Divide players into groups based on position where appropriate.
Allocate four minutes at each station.
Allow 60 seconds to rotate.
Use assessment categories covering effort quality, movement purpose, skill execution, recovery and decision making.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete the Midfield Exit station.
Groups rotate to the Forward Pressure station.
Players complete the Defensive Rebound station.
At the Position-Specific station, players complete the movement task suited to their role.
All players finish in the Three-Phase Transition Game.
Coaches record individual and group performance.
Players walk during every rotation.
Complete all five stations.
Allow three minutes recovery.
Repeat selected stations where further evidence is required.
Finish with feedback identifying one movement strength and one conditioning priority.
coachingPoints: Assess whether every running effort has a football purpose.
Record acceleration, braking and repositioning quality.
Observe whether players remain involved after disposal.
Assess role-specific repeat efforts.
Monitor transition reaction.
Include football skill and decision quality in every score.
Assess recovery behaviour between efforts.
Compare results with appropriate positional and individual expectations.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether midfielders exit congestion effectively.
Whether forwards transition from pressure to attack.
Whether defenders rebound and recover.
Whether position-specific efforts remain consistent.
Whether players recognise phase changes.
Whether football skill survives fatigue.
Whether recovery habits prepare the next effort.
Whether players communicate throughout.

commonErrors.error: Assessment becomes a running-speed test only.
commonErrors.correction: Score football purpose, skill, decision making and recovery separately.

commonErrors.error: All players complete identical positional tasks.
commonErrors.correction: Use role-specific options at the fourth station.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt maximal effort at every station.
commonErrors.correction: Explain the target intensity and purpose of each activity.

commonErrors.error: Coaches overlook recovery behaviour.
commonErrors.correction: Include recovery and reset as a scored category.

commonErrors.error: Players lose technique late in the assessment.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce station duration or increase rotation recovery.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is too general.
commonErrors.correction: Provide one observable strength and one specific development priority.

progressions: Add live opposition at selected stations.
Reduce rotation recovery.
Use positional benchmarks.
Record repeat-effort consistency and skill accuracy.
Repeat the assessment after a targeted training phase.
successIndicators: Repeat efforts appropriate to their role.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can translate conditioning into meaningful Australian football actions, including congestion exits, forward pressure, defensive rebound, positional repeat efforts and continuous transition between phases.

title: Chase, Pressure and Re-Engage
objective: Develop the ability to complete an effective chasing effort, apply controlled pressure and recover quickly enough to influence the next possession.
groundSize: Four to six lanes measuring 30 metres by 10 metres.
equipment: Two coloured pressure gates per lane
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a starting cone at one end of each lane.
Place an attacking player five metres ahead of a defender.
Position a feeder on the side of the lane.
Mark two pressure gates near the far end.
Place a second receiver beyond the gates.
Use 20–25-second work periods with 45–60 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins carrying or receiving the football while moving forward.
The defender chases from five metres behind.
The defender closes space and applies controlled pressure without making unsafe contact.
The attacker disposes to the receiver beyond one pressure gate.
The defender immediately changes direction and re-engages by chasing the receiver.
The receiver carries the football for five metres before disposing back to the feeder.
The defender continues until the final disposal is completed.
Players walk back outside the lane.
Rotate attacker, defender and receiver roles.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Accelerate immediately from the starting position.
Run towards the attacker’s escape line rather than directly behind them.
Shorten steps when approaching pressure distance.
Maintain balance and avoid overrunning possession.
Use voice and body position to influence the disposal.
React immediately after the first disposal.
Re-accelerate towards the second receiver.
Preserve pressure technique as fatigue increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender accelerates with intent.
Whether the approach remains controlled.
Whether the defender influences the first disposal.
Whether the second chase begins immediately.
Whether technique deteriorates across repeated efforts.

commonErrors.error: Defender runs directly behind the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Angle the chase towards the likely disposal lane.

commonErrors.error: Defender overruns the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten steps and lower the hips before applying pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after the first disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Make the second chase a compulsory scoring component.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches or makes unsafe contact.
commonErrors.correction: Use coralling and legal pressure rather than lunging.

commonErrors.error: Final repetitions become token efforts.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery or reduce the number of repetitions.

progressions: Reduce the defender’s starting disadvantage.
Allow the attacker to choose either gate.
Add a third possession and pressure effort.
Introduce controlled tackling for appropriate groups.
Reduce recovery between repetitions.
successIndicators: Complete repeated chases with consistent intent.
matchApplication: Defensive pressure often requires more than one chase. Players must influence the first possession and continue working to affect the next receiver rather than stopping after the football is released.

title: Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit
objective: Develop the ability to perform repeated legal tackling actions, regain the feet and contribute to the next football effort.
groundSize: Four to six stations measuring 15 metres by 10 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place a tackle bag or controlled ball carrier five metres from the start cone.
Mark a recovery cone three metres beyond the tackle point.
Position a feeder and receiver on opposite sides of the station.
Organise groups of three or four.
Use three-contact sequences with 60–75 seconds recovery.
Establish legal tackling and release rules before beginning.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working player accelerates from the start cone.
The player completes a controlled tackle on the bag or ball carrier.
The player releases immediately on the coach’s call.
The player regains balance and moves around the recovery cone.
The feeder delivers a ground ball or handball.
The player collects and handballs to the receiver.
The player returns for the next tackling effort.
Complete three tackle-and-release efforts.
Rotate roles during recovery.
Complete three or four sequences each.
coachingPoints: Track the hips of the ball carrier.
Approach with short, balanced steps.
Make contact below the shoulders and above the knees.
Keep the head to the safe side.
Drive with the legs rather than swinging the opponent.
Release immediately when instructed.
Regain the feet quickly after contact.
Maintain clean football skill after the tackling effort.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the approach is balanced.
Whether contact remains legal and controlled.
Whether the player releases safely.
Whether the player regains the feet efficiently.
Whether skill execution remains clean after contact.

commonErrors.error: Player approaches too upright.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Head is placed in front of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Move the head to the safe side of the body.

commonErrors.error: Player uses arms without leg drive.
commonErrors.correction: Wrap securely and continue driving through the feet.

commonErrors.error: Player remains on the ground after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Practise a quick safe release and get-up technique.

commonErrors.error: Contact quality declines late in the sequence.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the sequence to two contacts or increase recovery.

progressions: Replace the tackle bag with a controlled moving ball carrier.
Add a second football action after the tackle.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Include a short chase before contact.
Add a legal tackle-to-ground finish for suitably trained senior groups.
regressions: Complete one controlled contact per repetition.
successIndicators: Execute the following football skill accurately.
matchApplication: Players must often tackle, release, regain their feet and immediately pressure or use the football again. This drill develops safe repeat-contact conditioning rather than isolated tackling technique.

title: Contested Ground-Ball Work-Rate Grid
objective: Develop the ability to contest repeated ground balls, protect possession and recover quickly for the next football.
groundSize: Two to four grids measuring 20 metres by 20 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place two players on opposite sides of each grid.
Position one feeder outside the grid.
Mark four outlet gates around the boundary.
Keep three footballs with the feeder.
Use three-ball sequences followed by 60 seconds recovery.
Establish controlled body-contact and no-diving rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the first football into the grid.
Both players compete to gain front position and collect.
The winner releases through any open outlet gate.
The other player applies controlled pressure until the disposal is completed.
Both players immediately recover towards the centre.
The feeder releases the second football in a different direction.
Repeat for three footballs.
Award one point for a clean win and one point for an accurate outlet.
Rotate one player after each sequence.
Complete four to six sequences.
coachingPoints: React to the football rather than guessing.
Approach with the body balanced.
Establish front position without illegal contact.
Keep the head over the football.
Protect possession with the hips and shoulders.
Release to the safest available gate.
Apply pressure after losing the contest.
Recover immediately for the next football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players attack the football safely.
Whether body positioning is legal.
Whether the winner releases cleanly.
Whether the losing player continues to pressure.
Whether both players recover for every repetition.

commonErrors.error: Players dive at the football.
commonErrors.correction: Stay on the feet and approach with controlled steps.

commonErrors.error: Contact occurs before either player is near the football.
commonErrors.correction: Compete for position within the legal contest area.

commonErrors.error: Winner holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the outlet gates before collecting.

commonErrors.error: Losing player stops after the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Award defensive points for forcing an error.

commonErrors.error: Players remain near the previous outlet.
commonErrors.correction: Require a central reset before the next football.

progressions: Add a support player outside each gate.
Allow the feeder to use bouncing footballs.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Add a fourth football.
Require the winner to follow the disposal and receive again.
matchApplication: Contested ground balls rarely occur once in isolation. Players must repeatedly compete, release, pressure and recover as the football moves through congestion.
relatedDrills: CF-042 – Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit

title: Pressured Exit Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to escape controlled pressure, identify an outlet and execute a clean disposal during repeated high-work efforts.
groundSize: Three to four grids measuring 25 metres by 20 metres.
equipment: Three coloured outlet gates per grid
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central possession box measuring eight metres by eight metres.
Place three outlet gates around the outside.
Organise groups of three: ball carrier, defender and support player.
Position the support player beyond one outlet gate.
Start the defender two metres from the ball carrier.
Use 20-second repetitions with 45–60 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier receives inside the central box.
The defender applies controlled pressure.
The ball carrier must evade, create separation and exit the box.
The support player moves between the outlet gates.
The ball carrier identifies the support player and disposes accurately.
The ball carrier follows the disposal for a return handball.
The defender continues pressure until the return possession is completed.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
Change the starting position and preferred exit side between rounds.
coachingPoints: Scan the outlet options before receiving.
Protect the football with the body.
Use a decisive first movement.
Avoid repeated evasive steps without forward progress.
Accelerate after creating separation.
Dispose to the support player’s advantage.
Continue moving after release.
Maintain decision quality as fatigue increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the player scans early.
Whether the football is protected legally.
Whether the evasion creates real separation.
Whether the correct outlet is selected.
Whether the defender maintains controlled pressure.
Whether skill quality survives repeated efforts.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier receives without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require the player to identify two outlets before possession.

commonErrors.error: Player evades sideways without escaping.
commonErrors.correction: Use one decisive movement followed by acceleration.

commonErrors.error: Football is carried away from the body.
commonErrors.correction: Keep it protected on the side away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Support player remains stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Move between gates and present a clear target.

commonErrors.error: Defender makes unsafe contact.
commonErrors.correction: Use touch or coralling pressure until control improves.

progressions: Add a second support player.
Allow the defender to tackle under controlled rules.
Reduce the central box size.
Add a second possession after the exit.
Reduce recovery between repetitions.
matchApplication: Players often receive in congestion and must escape pressure before releasing to a teammate. This drill combines evasion, decision making and repeat conditioning in a realistic possession problem.

title: Spoil, Recover and Rebound Efforts
objective: Develop the ability to complete an aerial defensive effort, recover at ground level and contribute to the rebound possession.
groundSize: Two to four channels measuring 30 metres by 15 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a feeder 20 metres from an aerial contest area.
Place one defender and one controlled marking target in the contest area.
Mark a rebound gate 15 metres away.
Position a support player near the rebound gate.
Use two-contest sequences with 60–75 seconds recovery.
Establish safe aerial-contact and landing rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the aerial contest.
The defender positions and spoils the football away from the target.
Both players land safely.
The defender immediately recovers towards the spoiled football.
A second feeder or coach rolls another football into the rebound lane.
The defender collects or receives and kicks through the rebound gate.
The defender follows the disposal for five metres.
Reset for the second aerial contest.
Rotate defender, target, support and feeder roles.
Complete three or four sequences each.
coachingPoints: Establish position before the football arrives.
Keep eyes on the football.
Spoil with a strong, controlled fist.
Direct the spoil away from dangerous central space.
Land with balance.
Recover immediately after the aerial effort.
Use clean hands at ground level.
Regain posture before the rebound kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender maintains safe body position.
Whether the spoil is directed effectively.
Whether landing remains balanced.
Whether recovery begins immediately.
Whether the rebound disposal remains accurate.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the opponent rather than the football.
commonErrors.correction: Reconnect vision with the football before jumping.

commonErrors.error: Spoil is directed back into the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Aim towards the boundary side or supporting defender.

commonErrors.error: Player lands stiff-legged.
commonErrors.correction: Use soft knees and balanced landing posture.

commonErrors.error: Defender pauses after the spoil.
commonErrors.correction: Make the ground recovery a scored component.

commonErrors.error: Rebound kick is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Take balanced control steps before disposal.

progressions: Add a live marking opponent.
Allow the support player to move between two gates.
Include a second aerial contest without full reset.
Reduce recovery.
Add controlled forward pressure on the rebound.
successIndicators: Repeat aerial efforts without technical decline.
matchApplication: Defenders must often spoil, land, recover and become part of the rebound. This drill conditions the complete defensive action rather than ending the effort at the spoil.

title: Contact-to-Skill Conditioning Lane
primarySkill: Executing football skills after controlled contact
objective: Develop the ability to absorb or apply legal controlled contact, regain balance and execute a clean football skill.
groundSize: Four to six lanes measuring 25 metres by eight metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a start cone, contact zone and disposal line.
Position a pad holder or controlled opponent in the contact zone.
Place a football beyond the contact point.
Mark one handball gate and one kicking gate.
Organise groups of three or four.
Use 20-second repetitions with 50–60 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The working player accelerates from the start cone.
The player enters the contact zone and completes a controlled bump-pad engagement or legal body-position contest.
The player separates and accelerates towards the football.
The player collects or receives.
The coach calls handball or kick.
The player executes through the correct target gate.
The player follows the disposal and slows under control.
Rotate worker, contact holder and feeder roles.
Complete four to six repetitions each.
Alternate contact sides between rounds.
coachingPoints: Enter contact with a strong, balanced base.
Keep the head and neck in safe alignment.
Use legal shoulder and body position.
Avoid charging or extending the arms.
Separate quickly after contact.
Regain balance before collecting.
Scan the disposal target.
Preserve skill technique after physical effort.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether contact remains legal and controlled.
Whether players maintain balance.
Whether acceleration resumes promptly.
Whether collection and disposal remain clean.
Whether fatigue increases unsafe contact.

commonErrors.error: Player charges into the pad.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce approach speed and establish a balanced contact position.

commonErrors.error: Arms extend into the opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Keep elbows controlled and use legal shoulder contact.

commonErrors.error: Player stumbles after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the base and lower the hips before engagement.

commonErrors.error: Player rushes the football pickup.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish posture before collecting.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes heavier across repetitions.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce intensity and reinforce technical limits.

progressions: Use a controlled live opponent.
Add a decision between two footballs.
Reduce recovery.
Require non-preferred-side disposal.
Add a second contact before possession.
matchApplication: Players often need to maintain balance through body contact before collecting or disposing. This drill develops the transition from physical contest to controlled football execution.
relatedDrills: CF-042 – Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit

title: Three-Effort Pressure Chain
objective: Develop the ability to complete three connected pressure actions without losing defensive technique or awareness.
groundSize: Four to five channels measuring 35 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Create three connected pressure stations in each channel:
Chase and corral
Smother or spoil pressure
Controlled tackle or touch finish
Organise groups of four or five.
Use one working defender at a time.
Allow 75–90 seconds recovery after each full chain.
Keep contact appropriate to age and skill level.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defender chases an attacker carrying the football for ten metres.
The defender corrals and forces a disposal.
The defender immediately changes direction towards a second attacker preparing to kick.
The defender applies controlled smother pressure.
A third ball carrier receives five metres away.
The defender closes and completes a controlled tackle or touch.
The defender releases and runs through the finish gate.
Rotate roles after each chain.
Complete three or four chains per player.
Record whether all three efforts are completed at the required standard.
coachingPoints: Treat every effort as connected.
Close space with speed but arrive under control.
Influence the first disposal rather than chasing blindly.
Keep hands low and safe when applying smother pressure.
Track the hips into the final tackle.
Maintain legal contact.
Continue working after an unsuccessful pressure action.
Provide full recovery between high-quality chains.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether effort two begins immediately.
Whether technique remains controlled.
Whether the defender maintains awareness of the next target.
Whether the final tackle remains legal.
Whether full-chain quality is repeatable.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops after influencing the first disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Direct attention immediately to the second attacker.

commonErrors.error: Smother attempt is reckless.
commonErrors.correction: Approach under control and keep hands below the kicking line.

commonErrors.error: Final tackle is made while off balance.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten steps before contact.

commonErrors.error: Player sacrifices technique for speed.
commonErrors.correction: Score each action for quality, not completion time alone.

commonErrors.error: Recovery is too short.
commonErrors.correction: Increase rest to preserve safe high-intensity effort.

progressions: Allow attackers to make live decisions.
Reduce recovery between chains.
Add a fourth pressure action.
Use a live legal tackle finish.
Begin the defender from a larger disadvantage.
regressions: Use a tackle bag at the final station.
matchApplication: High-value defensive passages often require several efforts in succession. This drill conditions players to chase, smother, tackle and continue working until the possession is resolved.
relatedDrills: CF-042 – Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit

title: Numbers-Down Recovery Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to recover, communicate and delay opposition ball movement when defending with fewer players.
groundSize: A 50-metre by 40-metre area with three scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Place three scoring gates across one end.
Organise four attackers against three defenders.
Start attackers near the halfway line.
Start two defenders inside the area and one recovery defender ten metres behind.
Use 20–30-second repetitions.
Rotate a fresh group after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attackers begin with possession and move towards the scoring gates.
The recovery defender sprints into the area from behind.
The two starting defenders delay the attack and protect the most dangerous gate.
The recovery defender communicates and takes the highest-priority opponent.
Attackers score by disposing through any gate.
