Defenders score by forcing a turnover, boundary exit or backward disposal.
If defenders win possession, they counter through the starting line.
Rotate groups after each repetition.
Complete six to ten repetitions.
Change the recovery defender’s starting position.
coachingPoints: Recover through the most dangerous central lane.
Communicate while running.
Delay rather than attempting an unrealistic immediate win.
Protect the corridor and nearest scoring gate.
Force attackers towards lower-value space.
Match up only when numbers allow.
Transition quickly if possession is won.
Use full-effort recovery within a short controlled repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the recovering defender chooses the correct line.
Whether starting defenders delay effectively.
Whether communication assigns opponents.
Whether defenders protect central space.
Whether fatigue affects decision quality.

commonErrors.error: Recovery defender runs directly to the football.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through the central scoring threat first.

commonErrors.error: Starting defenders charge at the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Hold distance and delay the possession.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain silent.
commonErrors.correction: Require early calls identifying gate and opponent priorities.

commonErrors.error: All defenders protect the same attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate ball, support and deepest threat roles.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after winning possession.
commonErrors.correction: Counter immediately through the starting line.

progressions: Increase the attacking advantage to five against three.
Allow unrestricted attacker movement.
Reduce defender recovery distance.
Add a second attacking phase after the first score attempt.
Reduce rest between repetitions.
regressions: Use three attackers against three defenders.
matchApplication: Turnovers often leave teams temporarily outnumbered. Defenders must recover, delay and protect dangerous space until teammates reconnect.

title: Chaos Ball Conditioning Game
primarySkill: Maintaining work rate and skill during unpredictable football
objective: Develop the ability to maintain effort, composure and football skill when possession becomes unpredictable and repeated contests occur.
groundSize: A 45-metre by 45-metre square.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two even teams.
Place one scoring gate on each side of the square.
Begin with one live football.
Keep two additional footballs with coaches outside the area.
Use two-minute playing periods with 90 seconds active recovery.
Establish controlled-contact and safe ground-ball rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams compete for possession and may score through any gate.
After a score, the coach immediately introduces another football from a different side.
At random moments, the coach may call “new ball” and release a second football while removing the first.
Players must react, reorganise and continue.
A turnover requires immediate transition.
A score is worth one point.
A score following three consecutive team pressure actions is worth two points.
Play for two minutes.
Walk, recover and review for 90 seconds.
Complete four to six periods.
coachingPoints: Remain aware of the coach and available footballs.
React to the current live football immediately.
Avoid diving into ground contests.
Communicate possession, pressure and support roles.
Spread after winning the football.
Collapse space after losing it.
Maintain legal controlled contact.
Use the recovery period to reset team roles.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify the live football.
Whether teams reorganise after sudden changes.
Whether ground-ball technique remains safe.
Whether support and pressure efforts continue.
Whether fatigue causes reckless decisions or contact.

commonErrors.error: Players continue chasing a dead football.
commonErrors.correction: Use a clear whistle and verbal live-ball call.

commonErrors.error: Too many players collapse around possession.
commonErrors.correction: Require outside support around the contest.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes uncontrolled.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce numbers, space or contact level immediately.

commonErrors.error: Players dispose without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Require one visible supporting option before release.

commonErrors.error: Work rate becomes frantic rather than purposeful.
commonErrors.correction: Reward effective pressure and possession structure, not random running.

progressions: Use two live footballs for a short controlled period.
Reduce playing area.
Add gate-specific scoring calls.
Shorten recovery periods.
Introduce scoreboard pressure.
matchApplication: Matches contain unpredictable bounces, repeated contests, turnovers and sudden changes of direction. This game conditions players to remain composed and effective when the football does not move as planned.

title: Pressure Conditioning Mid-Chapter Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated assessment of conditioning under pressure and contest
objective: Assess whether players can maintain safe movement, repeat effort, decision quality and football skill during pressured and contested conditioning activities.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval divided into five assessment stations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create five assessment stations:
Chase and Re-Engage
Tackle, Release and Recover
Contested Ground-Ball Sequence
Pressure Exit and Defensive Recovery
Chaos Conditioning Game
Divide players into groups appropriate to age, size and position.
Allocate three minutes at each technical station.
Use a four-minute final game.
Allow 60–75 seconds to rotate.
Assess effort quality, safety, football skill, recovery and decision making.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete repeated chasing and re-engagement efforts.
At the tackle station, players demonstrate safe contact, release and recovery.
At the ground-ball station, players compete through a three-football sequence.
At the pressure station, players exit congestion and then recover defensively.
All players finish in the Chaos Conditioning Game.
Coaches record individual and group performance.
Players walk during station rotations.
Complete every station.
Allow three minutes active recovery.
Repeat selected activities where further assessment is required.
Finish with feedback on one pressure-conditioning strength and one development priority.
coachingPoints: Assess technique and football purpose, not fatigue alone.
Stop any station where contact becomes unsafe.
Observe whether players repeat efforts after an initial action.
Record ground-ball and disposal quality under pressure.
Assess defensive recovery lines.
Monitor decision making as fatigue increases.
Include recovery behaviour between efforts.
Apply age, role and training-status adjustments.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether chasing efforts remain controlled.
Whether tackling technique is legal and safe.
Whether players compete at ground level without diving.
Whether football skills remain effective after contact.
Whether defensive recovery decisions are sound.
Whether players maintain composure during unpredictable play.
Whether recovery supports the next effort.
Whether workloads are appropriate for each player.

commonErrors.error: Players treat the assessment as a collision contest.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that safe technique and football outcome are the priorities.

commonErrors.error: Coaches assess effort without skill quality.
commonErrors.correction: Score physical effort and football execution separately.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after their first action.
commonErrors.correction: Include repeat involvement as an assessment category.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes unsafe ground-ball technique.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration or contact immediately.

commonErrors.error: All players are assessed against identical contact loads.
commonErrors.correction: Modify by age, size, position and training status.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is vague.
commonErrors.correction: Provide one observable strength and one specific improvement action.

progressions: Add controlled live opposition at each station.
Reduce rotation recovery.
Introduce positional assessment standards.
Record repeat-effort consistency and disposal accuracy.
Repeat the assessment after a dedicated pressure-conditioning block.
regressions: Replace live contact with bags or shadow pressure.
successIndicators: Repeat efforts after the first action.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can sustain the physical and technical demands of chasing, tackling, contesting, recovering and using the football during repeated pressured passages of Australian football.
relatedDrills: CF-042 – Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit
CF-045 – Spoil, Recover and Rebound Efforts

title: Repeat Smother and Recovery Run
objective: Develop the ability to close a kicker safely, apply effective smother pressure and recover immediately to influence the next possession.
groundSize: Four to six lanes measuring 25 metres by eight metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a defender’s starting cone ten metres behind a kicker.
Place a disposal line five metres in front of the kicker.
Position a second receiver ten metres beyond the disposal line.
Place a recovery football beside the lane.
Organise groups of three or four.
Use three-effort sequences with 60 seconds recovery.
Establish clear rules preventing contact with the kicker’s leg or body.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker begins moving towards the disposal line.
The defender accelerates from behind and closes the space.
The kicker completes a controlled kick before the line.
The defender applies smother pressure with hands extended safely below the kicking line.
Immediately after the kick, the coach releases a second football into the lane.
The defender changes direction, collects the football and handballs through a target gate.
The defender then recovers to the starting cone.
Repeat the sequence three times.
Rotate defender, kicker and receiver roles.
Complete three or four sequences per player.
coachingPoints: Accelerate strongly during the early chase.
Decelerate before entering the kicker’s space.
Keep the body balanced and avoid diving.
Extend the hands without making contact with the kicking leg.
Watch the football leave the kicker’s hands.
React immediately to the second football.
Collect under control before releasing.
Recover to the starting position with purpose.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender closes space quickly.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether smother technique remains safe.
Whether the defender reacts immediately after the kick.
Whether the recovery handball remains accurate.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives at the kicker.
commonErrors.correction: Stay on the feet and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Hands rise towards the kicker’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Extend towards the football’s release point only.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops after the kick.
commonErrors.correction: Introduce the second football immediately.

commonErrors.error: Ground-ball collection is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and collect before releasing.

commonErrors.error: Repeated efforts become unsafe.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery or reduce sequence length.

progressions: Allow the kicker to use either foot.
Add a live choice between two recovery footballs.
Reduce the defender’s starting distance.
Add a second pressure action after the handball.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
successIndicators: React immediately to the second football.
matchApplication: Players must often pressure a kick and then immediately recover to contest a loose football or influence the next possession. This drill conditions both actions as one continuous defensive effort.
relatedDrills: CF-042 – Repeat Tackle and Release Circuit

title: Boundary Trap Repeat Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to use the boundary as an additional defender, apply repeated pressure and prevent an easy exit.
groundSize: Two to four boundary channels measuring 25 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use a boundary line or mark one side of each channel as the boundary.
Place an attacking player five metres inside the boundary.
Position two defenders ten metres away.
Mark one inside exit gate at the opposite end.
Position a feeder outside the channel.
Use 20-second repetitions with 50–60 seconds recovery.
Apply controlled tackling rules appropriate to the group.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder delivers the football to the attacker near the boundary.
The first defender closes from the inside and prevents the attacker moving centrally.
The second defender supports from behind or ahead to close the escape route.
The attacker attempts to carry or dispose through the inside exit gate.
Defenders score by forcing a boundary disposal, turnover or delayed possession.
If the attacker escapes, both defenders chase and re-engage.
The repetition ends after the attacker exits or possession is lost.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
Change the starting position and pressure angle between rounds.
coachingPoints: Approach from the inside to protect central space.
Use the boundary to limit the attacker’s options.
Avoid both defenders attacking from the same angle.
Communicate who pressures and who covers.
Maintain balanced footwork.
Tackle legally when the opportunity appears.
Continue chasing if the first trap is broken.
Recover to starting positions during the rest period.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders protect the corridor side.
Whether their angles complement each other.
Whether communication occurs before contact.
Whether the attacker is forced towards the boundary.
Whether defenders continue after the first effort.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders chase from directly behind.
commonErrors.correction: Place one defender inside and one covering the forward exit.

commonErrors.error: First defender overcommits.
commonErrors.correction: Corral and delay until support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain silent.
commonErrors.correction: Require an early pressure-and-cover call.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes unsafe near the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and use touch pressure until control improves.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop when the attacker escapes.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the repetition live until the exit gate is crossed.

progressions: Add a support attacker inside the field.
Use live tackling for suitably trained groups.
Reduce the channel width.
Add a second escape gate.
Reduce recovery between repetitions.
regressions: Use one defender and one passive cover player.
matchApplication: Teams frequently defend near the boundary, where effective positioning can remove one side of the field. This drill develops the repeated work and coordination required to trap possession outside.
relatedDrills: CF-051 – Repeat Smother and Recovery Run

title: Press, Turnover and Counter Run
primarySkill: Transitioning from team pressure to counterattack
objective: Develop the ability to apply coordinated team pressure and immediately accelerate into attacking support after winning possession.
groundSize: A 50-metre by 40-metre area with two counterattack gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise four attackers against four defenders.
Begin the attacking team with possession inside a 25-metre central zone.
Place two counterattack gates beyond each end.
Position one neutral feeder outside the area.
Use 30-second repetitions followed by 60 seconds recovery.
Rotate a fresh group after each repetition where squad numbers allow.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team attempts to complete six possessions.
The defending team applies coordinated pressure and attempts to force a turnover.
If the defenders win possession, they immediately counterattack towards either gate.
The former attackers must transition to defence.
The counterattack ends when the football passes through a gate or possession is lost.
If six possessions are completed, the feeder introduces a loose football to create a turnover contest.
Both teams continue until the counterattack is resolved.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
Complete six to ten repetitions.
Award one point for a forced turnover and one point for a successful counterattack.
coachingPoints: Press as a connected unit rather than as isolated chasers.
Close the most dangerous disposal lanes.
Communicate pressure and cover roles.
React immediately when possession changes.
Spread quickly after winning the football.
Use the first clean option rather than overhandling.
Continue running after the first counterattack disposal.
Recover actively between repetitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders pressure as a unit.
Whether the turnover is followed by immediate spread.
Whether the first disposal is clean.
Whether former attackers transition defensively.
Whether repeated pressure efforts remain coordinated.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase individually.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain spacing and close options around the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: Players celebrate or pause after winning possession.
commonErrors.correction: Make the counterattack gate the immediate objective.

commonErrors.error: All counterattack runners follow the football.
commonErrors.correction: Use inside, outside and forward support lanes.

commonErrors.error: Former attackers fail to recover.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the repetition live until the gate is crossed.

commonErrors.error: First disposal after turnover is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the nearest clean support option.

progressions: Reduce the playing area.
Add a fifth attacker.
Limit counterattack time.
Add a second possession after crossing the gate.
Reduce recovery between repetitions.
successIndicators: Transition defensively when possession is lost.
matchApplication: Effective teams convert pressure into scoring opportunities. This drill conditions players to move immediately from defensive work into attacking support once the turnover is created.

title: Pack Exit Repeat Contest
primarySkill: Repeated exit from a congested pack
objective: Develop the ability to repeatedly win or support possession in congestion and create a clean exit through body positioning and rapid disposal.
groundSize: Two to four grids measuring 22 metres by 22 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a six-metre central contest circle.
Place four outlet gates around the outside.
Organise teams of two against two.
Position a feeder with three footballs.
Use three-football sequences with 75 seconds recovery.
Establish clear rules for legal bodywork and safe ground-ball contests.
howTheDrillWorks:
All four players begin inside the contest circle.
The feeder releases the first football.
Players compete to win possession or support the winner.
The team in possession must exit through any gate.
The supporting player may block legally or receive a handball.
Once the football exits, all players recover to the circle.
The feeder immediately releases the second football.
Complete three contests in one sequence.
Rotate teams or players during recovery.
Complete four to six sequences.
coachingPoints: Stay on the feet whenever possible.
Establish body position before reaching for the football.
Communicate who wins and who supports.
Use legal blocks to create an exit lane.
Release the football quickly after possession is secured.
Accelerate through the gate.
Re-centre immediately after each contest.
Maintain composure as fatigue builds.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players compete safely.
Whether teammates coordinate possession and support roles.
Whether legal bodywork creates space.
Whether the exit disposal is clean.
Whether all players recover for each football.

commonErrors.error: Both teammates dive on the football.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one winner and one support player.

commonErrors.error: Players hold possession in congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Scan outlets before the football is won.

commonErrors.error: Blocking becomes holding or pushing.
commonErrors.correction: Use legal body positioning with arms controlled.

commonErrors.error: Players remain outside after an exit.

title: Aerial Contest to Ground Pressure Chain

Place a second football with a coach near ground level.
Mark an outlet gate ten metres away.
Use two-contest sequences with 75 seconds recovery.
Establish safe aerial-bodywork, landing and tackling rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks to the aerial contest.
The attacker attempts to mark while the defender spoils or competes legally.
Both players land and immediately locate the football.
If the mark is completed, the defender applies controlled pressure.

The coach then introduces the second football into a different space.
Both players complete a second ground-level effort.
The winner exits through the outlet gate.
Rotate roles after each sequence.
Complete three or four sequences per player.
coachingPoints: Maintain eyes on the football during the aerial contest.
Use legal body position.
Land with balance and soft knees.
React immediately after landing.
Stay on the feet at ground level.
Protect possession before releasing.

Preserve technique across repeated efforts.

Whether aerial contact remains legal.
Whether players land safely.
Whether reaction after landing is immediate.
Whether ground-ball technique remains controlled.
Whether the second effort matches the first.

title: Defensive Repeat Close-Out Grid

Place one cone in the centre and four receiver cones around the outside.
Position one defender at the centre.
Place one receiver at each outside cone.
Give one receiver the football.
Use 25-second work periods with 50 seconds recovery.
Apply no-contact or touch-pressure rules.
howTheDrillWorks:
The outside players pass the football around the grid.
The defender closes the current receiver.
The defender must decelerate before reaching pressure distance.
As the football is passed, the defender recovers towards the centre.
The defender then accelerates towards the next receiver.
Outside players may use kick or handball depending on distance.
Continue for 25 seconds.
Rotate the defender.
Complete four to six work periods per player.
Vary the passing direction and speed.

Accelerate strongly from the central position.
Shorten steps during the final approach.
Arrive balanced enough to react.
Angle the close-out to protect the dangerous side.
Recover towards the centre after every disposal.
Communicate with nearby defenders where multiple grids are combined.
Maintain technique rather than chasing every possession recklessly.

Whether the final approach remains controlled.
Whether the correct side is protected.
Whether recovery returns through the centre.

Position a feeder at one end of each channel.

Match players by appropriate size and ability.

The attacker and defender begin side by side.
On the feeder’s cue, both players lead towards the first contest point.
The feeder kicks to advantage or neutral space.
Players compete for the mark or spoil.
Both players land and recover around the outside cone.
The feeder immediately directs them towards the second contest point.
A second kick is delivered.
After the second contest, players walk through recovery.
Rotate feeder and player roles where appropriate.
Complete three or four sequences each.
coachingPoints: Establish position early without holding.
Track the football throughout the flight.
Use legal body contact.
Attack the football at the highest safe point.
Land with balance.
Recover immediately after the first contest.
Approach the second effort with the same technique.
Stop the drill if aerial quality or safety declines.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether body contact remains legal.
Whether players maintain visual connection with the football.
Whether landing is safe.
Whether the second lead has strong intent.
Whether fatigue affects aerial technique.

title: Stoppage Pressure Rotation
primarySkill: Repeated pressure and role rotation at stoppage
objective: Develop the ability to complete repeated stoppage pressure actions while rotating between ball-winning, support and defensive roles.
groundSize: Two to four stoppage grids measuring 22 metres by 22 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise teams of three against three.
Mark a central stoppage circle.
Place four outlet gates around the grid.
Position a feeder with two footballs.
Assign initial roles: ball winner, support player and defensive cover.
Use two-stoppage sequences with 75 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder throws or bounces the football into the stoppage.
Players compete to win or pressure possession.
The team in possession attempts to exit through any gate.
The defending team tackles, blocks and closes outlets.
Once the football exits or possession is lost, all players return to the centre.
Players rotate roles within their team.
The feeder immediately begins the second stoppage.
After two stoppages, teams walk through recovery.
Rotate opponents or starting roles.
Complete four to six sequences.
coachingPoints: Enter the contest with a clear role.
Communicate who wins, supports and covers.
Apply legal pressure around the football.
Keep feet moving in congestion.
Use body positioning to protect or block.
Release possession quickly when an outlet appears.
Rotate roles before the second stoppage.
Maintain structure despite fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players perform their assigned role.
Whether roles rotate effectively.
Whether contact remains controlled.
Whether outlet decisions are quick.
Whether the second stoppage retains structure.

commonErrors.correction: Maintain one winner, one support player and one defensive cover.

commonErrors.error: Players hold possession too long.

commonErrors.error: Blocking becomes illegal holding.

title: Pressure Wave Survival Game
primarySkill: Maintaining possession through repeated pressure waves
objective: Develop the ability to survive repeated defensive pressure waves while preserving possession structure, decision quality and work rate.
groundSize: A 55-metre by 45-metre area divided into three zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise one possession team of eight to ten players.
Organise two pressure groups of four to six players.
Place the possession team inside the full area.
Begin one pressure group in the first zone.
Keep the second pressure group resting outside.
Mark two exit gates at each end.
Use 45-second pressure waves.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins with the football and attempts to move through all three zones.
The first pressure group enters and applies full controlled pressure for 45 seconds.
The possession team scores by exiting through an end gate.
At the end of the first wave, the pressure group exits immediately.
The second pressure group enters from a different side.
The possession team must reorganise and continue without a full stoppage.
Complete three consecutive pressure waves.
The possession team then walks and recovers for two minutes.
Rotate teams after each full set.
Complete three or four sets.
coachingPoints: Maintain width and depth under pressure.
Use short support options around possession.
Move immediately after disposal.
Change the point of attack when pressure compresses one side.
Communicate before each pressure wave arrives.
Avoid forcing low-percentage disposals.
Use brief low-pressure moments to reset structure.
Preserve running and skill quality across all waves.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the possession team maintains structure.
Whether support movement continues under fatigue.
Whether decisions become rushed.
Whether each pressure group enters with coordinated intensity.
Whether the possession team uses brief recovery opportunities.

commonErrors.error: Possession team collapses around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain outside width and one central support option.

commonErrors.error: Players stand after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate replacement movement.

commonErrors.error: Disposal becomes rushed after the second wave.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest clean option and change the point of attack.

commonErrors.error: Pressure groups chase individually.
commonErrors.correction: Enter as a connected wave with assigned roles.

Reduce the possession-team numbers.

title: Pressure and Contest Block Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated assessment of pressure and contested conditioning
objective: Assess whether players can apply safe, repeatable and football-effective pressure and contest behaviours across multiple high-work scenarios.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval divided into six assessment stations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create six assessment stations:
Smother and Recovery
Boundary Pressure Trap
Congestion Exit
Aerial-to-Ground Contest
Stoppage Pressure Rotation
Pressure Wave Survival Game
Divide players into groups based on age, position and contact readiness.

Allow 60–75 seconds to rotate.
Assess effort quality, safety, football execution, decision making, repeatability and recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:

Coaches record performance against controlled assessment criteria.
Players walk during all station rotations.
Complete every station.
Allow three minutes active recovery.
Repeat any station requiring further evidence.
Finish with individual and team feedback.
coachingPoints: Assess effective football pressure rather than effort volume alone.
Stop any activity where contact or movement becomes unsafe.
Record whether players repeat effort after the first action.
Include disposal and decision quality in every assessment.
Observe whether players remain balanced when closing space.
Assess role understanding within congestion and stoppages.
Monitor active recovery and preparation for the next station.
Modify contact and workload for age, position and training status.

Whether smother pressure is safe and effective.
Whether defenders use the boundary correctly.
Whether players exit congestion with support.
Whether aerial contests transition into ground effort.
Whether stoppage roles remain organised.

title: Outnumber Creation Repeat Runs
primarySkill: Repeated running to create attacking outnumbers
objective: Develop the ability to complete repeated supporting runs that create an attacking numerical advantage and continue into the next phase of possession.
groundSize: A 50-metre by 35-metre area divided into three horizontal zones.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the area into starting, support and finishing zones.
Organise groups of four attackers and three defenders.
Place two attackers and two defenders in the starting zone.
Position one attacker and one defender in the support zone.
Place the fourth attacker outside the starting zone as the outnumber runner.
Mark two scoring gates at the far end.
Use 30-second repetitions with 60 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
Two attackers begin with possession against two defenders in the starting zone.
The outside runner enters on the coach’s signal and accelerates past possession.
The attacking team uses the temporary outnumber to move into the support zone.
The support-zone attacker joins the possession while the defender attempts to delay.
The original outnumber runner continues forward to provide another option.
The attacking team scores by disposing through either end gate.
If the defenders win possession, they counter through the starting line.
All players recover to their starting positions.
Rotate the outnumber runner after each repetition.
Complete six to ten repetitions.
coachingPoints: Time the supporting run rather than leaving too early.
Accelerate past possession to create a genuine numerical advantage.
Use the free player quickly before the defence adjusts.
Maintain width between supporting runners.
Continue moving after the first disposal.
Communicate which player is free.
Finish the attack with a balanced disposal.
Recover actively before the next repetition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the outnumber runner enters at the correct time.
Whether attackers recognise the free player.
Whether the first supporting run continues into the next zone.
Whether defenders delay rather than overcommit.
Whether running and disposal quality remain consistent.

commonErrors.correction: Delay the run until the ball carrier can see and use the option.

commonErrors.error: Attackers crowd the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate inside, outside and forward support lanes.

commonErrors.error: Free player is ignored.
commonErrors.correction: Require the first or second disposal to use the outnumber.

matchApplication: Attacking outnumbers are created when players run beyond possession and remain involved through multiple phases. This drill conditions players to create and use the extra number rather than stopping after one support action.

title: Corridor Surge Endurance
primarySkill: Repeated high-speed support through the corridor
objective: Develop the ability to accelerate through the corridor, support forward possession and recover into a connected position for repeated attacking waves.
groundSize: A 75-metre by 45-metre area with a 15-metre-wide central corridor.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central corridor running the full length of the area.
Place outside possession stations on both sides.

Add one passive or controlled defender in the corridor.
Use staggered starts for multiple groups.
Mark an outside recovery lane along one boundary.

Possession begins at an outside station.
The corridor runner starts at controlled pace behind the football.
As the outside player prepares to dispose, the corridor runner accelerates into central space.
The runner receives and immediately releases forward by handball or kick.
The outside players continue running to support the next possession.
The group finishes with a kick through the scoring gate.
All players recover through the outside lane.
The next group begins when the first group clears the corridor.

Walk for 60 seconds and repeat for four work periods.

Accelerate decisively through central space.
Receive on the move.
Avoid carrying the football unnecessarily in the corridor.
Continue running after disposal.
Maintain outside support on both sides.
Use the recovery lane to return without disrupting play.
Preserve skill quality during later waves.

title: Defensive Press Reset Runs
primarySkill: Repeated defensive pressing and structural reset
objective: Develop the ability to press possession as a team, recover when the press is broken and reset defensive structure for the next attacking wave.
groundSize: A 65-metre by 50-metre area divided into three defensive lines.

setup:
Organise one possession team of seven to nine players.

The defending team presses forward when the ball carrier is restricted.

groundSize: Full oval or a minimum area of 120 metres by 70 metres.

Create five linked possession stations from defensive 50 to forward 50.
