commonErrors.correction: Add footballs or reduce players per station.

commonErrors.error: Recovery runners enter the active corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Use the designated outside return path.

commonErrors.error: Kicking distance becomes unrealistic under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten station spacing or increase recovery.

progressions: Add passive defenders at selected stations.
Allow live choice between inside and outside options.
Reduce recovery between work periods.
Add a turnover and defensive recovery phase.
Use two footballs moving in the same direction.
regressions: Use handball support only at selected stations.
successIndicators: Execute clean skills across repeated chains.
matchApplication: Players must remain connected to possession as it moves from defence to attack. This drill develops the sustained running and repeat support required to move the football across the ground.

title: Turnover Sprint and Outlet
objective: Develop the ability to react immediately to a turnover, sprint into a useful position and either defend or provide an attacking outlet.
groundSize: A 55-metre by 45-metre area with four outlet gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise two teams of five or six.
Begin with controlled possession in the central area.
Place one outlet gate on each side and end.
Keep additional footballs with the coach.
Use 30-second repetitions and 60–75 seconds recovery.
Nominate two starting players from each team as high or deep players.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins in controlled possession.
The coach calls “turnover” and releases a new football into a different area.
Both teams react immediately.
The team nearest the new football attempts to secure possession.
Teammates sprint to provide inside, outside and forward outlets.
The opposition recovers to protect the most dangerous gates.
The possession team scores by exiting through any gate.
The defending team scores by winning possession and countering.
Rotate starting positions after each repetition.
Complete six to ten repetitions.
coachingPoints: React to the turnover call without hesitation.
Sprint the first five metres.
Run to a useful role rather than directly towards the football.
Provide multiple outlet angles.
Defenders recover through central space.
Communicate possession and defensive roles.
Complete the first disposal cleanly.
Recover actively between repetitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players react immediately.
Whether support runners create useful outlets.
Whether defenders protect central gates.
Whether the first possession is controlled.
Whether effort remains consistent across repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Every player runs directly to the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate ball, inside support, outside support and defensive cover roles.

commonErrors.error: Players react slowly to the turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Use a clear whistle and score reaction speed.

commonErrors.error: Defenders recover towards the boundary side only.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor and deepest gate first.

commonErrors.error: First disposal is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and use the nearest clean outlet.

commonErrors.error: Later repetitions lose intensity.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery or reduce total repetitions.

progressions: Remove the verbal turnover call and use a visual cue.
Add a second live football.
Reduce recovery.
Limit the time available to exit.
Add scoreboard scenarios.
regressions: Use one team with an attacking numerical advantage.
matchApplication: Turnovers create short periods where both teams must sprint into new roles. The speed and purpose of the first reaction often determine whether the turnover becomes a scoring opportunity or defensive threat.
relatedDrills: CF-053 – Press, Turnover and Counter Run

title: Red-Time Possession Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession, control running output and make low-risk decisions during the final minutes of a quarter or match.
groundSize: A 55-metre by 45-metre area divided into four possession zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise a possession team with one extra player.
Divide the area into four zones.
Display a countdown period of 60–90 seconds.
Give the possession team a small scoreboard lead.
Set a disposal target or requirement to use all four zones.
Use 90-second scenarios with 90 seconds active recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins with the football and a simulated narrow lead.
The team attempts to retain possession until the clock expires.
Players must continue providing support but avoid unnecessary maximal running.
The defending team applies controlled pressure and attempts to force a turnover.
A turnover allows the defenders to score through either end gate.
The possession team may use a backwards or lateral disposal when appropriate.
If the football leaves the area, the coach restarts quickly.
Complete the 60–90-second scenario.
Walk, recover and review the decisions.
Swap roles and repeat four to six scenarios.
coachingPoints: Maintain width and multiple short options.
Use controlled running between decisive efforts.
Avoid forcing the football through congestion.
Continue moving after disposal.
Communicate time, score and available options.
Use safe backward or lateral possession when appropriate.
Recognise when to slow or accelerate play.
Recover actively between scenarios.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the scoreboard scenario.
Whether running remains purposeful.
Whether possession structure survives fatigue.
Whether communication includes time and score.
Whether players select low-risk options appropriately.

commonErrors.error: Players attack forward unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that retaining possession is the priority.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand still.
commonErrors.correction: Continue replacing positions after disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players sprint continuously and lose spacing.
commonErrors.correction: Use controlled movement until a decisive run is required.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers ignore the clock.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate a leader to communicate remaining time.

commonErrors.error: Possession becomes trapped on one side.
commonErrors.correction: Switch through the nearest safe option.

progressions: Remove the numerical advantage.
Reduce the playing area.
Increase defensive pressure.
Add a rule requiring one aggressive attacking option if available.
Use changing score and time scenarios.
successIndicators: Retain possession until the scenario ends.
matchApplication: Late in quarters, players must manage fatigue, field position, score and time. Effective conditioning includes the ability to keep moving intelligently rather than simply running at maximum speed.

title: Scoreboard Scenario Repeat Efforts
primarySkill: Adjusting repeat efforts to scoreboard scenarios
objective: Develop the ability to adjust running intensity, risk and team positioning according to changing score and time scenarios.
groundSize: A 70-metre by 55-metre area with two scoring zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two even teams.
Set up two scoring zones.
Prepare scenario cards such as:
Three points ahead with 90 seconds remaining.
Five points behind with 60 seconds remaining.
Scores level with one final possession.
Seven points ahead after a turnover.
Use 60–120-second scenarios with 90 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, time and starting possession.
Teams organise their structure.
Play begins immediately.
Players adjust running and risk according to the scenario.
The team behind must create forward movement and repeat support efforts.
The team ahead must defend dangerous space and retain possession when possible.
The scenario ends when time expires, a decisive score occurs or possession becomes dead.
Teams walk and review for 90 seconds.
Change the scenario and starting positions.
Complete five to eight scenarios.
coachingPoints: Know the score and time before the first movement.
Match running intensity to the team’s tactical need.
Protect dangerous central space when defending a lead.
Provide aggressive forward support when behind.
Use possession and field position intelligently.
Communicate tactical priorities.
Maintain clean skill under emotional and physical pressure.
Reset quickly for each new scenario.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand each scenario.
Whether running behaviour changes appropriately.
Whether teams maintain tactical structure.
Whether communication is specific to score and time.
Whether fatigue causes poor risk decisions.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same approach in every scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Pause and clarify the specific tactical objective.

commonErrors.error: Team ahead attacks recklessly.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise safe possession and field position.

commonErrors.error: Team behind moves the football too slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Increase forward running and play on from marks.

commonErrors.error: Defenders protect the boundary instead of the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Defend the highest-value scoring space first.

commonErrors.error: Players forget the remaining time.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one leader to call the countdown.

progressions: Remove coach reminders after the scenario begins.
Add interchange restrictions.
Use uneven numbers.
Introduce wet-weather or restricted-disposal rules.
Link two scenarios without full recovery.
regressions: Allow coaches to freeze and correct positioning.
successIndicators: Complete repeat efforts that suit the scenario.
matchApplication: Physical effort must serve the match situation. Players need to run differently when protecting a lead, chasing a score or managing the final possession.

title: Tactical Load Wave Game
objective: Develop the ability to repeatedly shift between high-pressure, controlled-possession and transition workloads while maintaining team structure.
groundSize: A 75-metre by 60-metre area divided into three horizontal zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two even teams.
Place two scoring gates at each end.
Prepare three phase calls:
Red: High-pressure live play.
Blue: Controlled possession.
Green: Immediate transition attack.
Use four-minute playing blocks.
Change phases every 20–45 seconds.
Allow 90 seconds active recovery between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in the Red phase with full controlled pressure.
On the Blue call, the team in possession attempts to retain the football at controlled tempo.
The opposition maintains shape but reduces pressure intensity.
On the Green call, the coach releases a second football or changes possession.
Both teams transition at high intensity towards the appropriate scoring gates.
The coach continues changing phases throughout the four-minute block.
Players must react without stopping play.
At the end of the block, players walk, recover and discuss phase recognition.
Swap starting possession.
Complete four to five blocks.
coachingPoints: Recognise the phase immediately.
Match physical intensity to the phase.
Maintain team shape during controlled possession.
Accelerate decisively during transition.
Avoid maximal running when the tactical demand is low.
Communicate phase changes.
Preserve disposal quality through workload changes.
Use recovery periods to reset physically and tactically.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise the current phase.
Whether running intensity changes appropriately.
Whether team structure remains connected.
Whether players transition together.
Whether skill quality survives repeated workload changes.
Whether recovery between blocks is effective.

commonErrors.error: Players remain at high intensity during every phase.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the specific physical target for each colour.

commonErrors.error: Controlled possession becomes stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Continue low-to-moderate support movement.

commonErrors.error: Transition begins slowly after the Green call.
commonErrors.correction: Demand an immediate first-five-metre reaction.

commonErrors.error: Teams lose shape during phase changes.
commonErrors.correction: Keep positional lines connected while adjusting intensity.

commonErrors.error: Players miss verbal phase calls.
commonErrors.correction: Add visible coloured cards or flags.

progressions: Remove the verbal call and use visual cues only.
Shorten the time between phase changes.
Add scoreboard scenarios.
Use uneven team numbers.
Reduce recovery between blocks.
matchApplication: A match alternates between intense pressure, controlled possession and rapid transition. Players must change physical output without losing tactical awareness or structure.

title: Advanced Football Conditioning Assessment
primarySkill: Integrated assessment of advanced football-conditioning application
objective: Assess whether players can apply advanced football-conditioning behaviours across attacking, defensive, transition and tactical scenarios.
groundSize: Approximately two-thirds to a full oval divided into six assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create six assessment zones:
Outnumber Creation
Corridor Surge
Defensive Press and Reset
Forward-Entry Repeat Waves
Turnover Sprint and Outlet
Tactical Scenario Game
Divide players into positional or balanced groups.
Allocate four minutes at Zones 1–5.
Use a six-minute final tactical game.
Allow 60–75 seconds between zones.
Assess football purpose, effort repeatability, structure, skill, decision making and recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete repeated outnumber-support runs.
Groups rotate to the corridor-surge station.
Players complete coordinated pressing and defensive reset efforts.
At the forward-entry station, players complete repeated lead, crumb and pressure waves.
At the turnover station, players react and sprint into new roles.
All players finish in the Tactical Scenario Game.
Coaches record individual and team behaviours.
Players walk during every station rotation.
Complete all six zones.
Allow three minutes active recovery.
Repeat selected zones where more evidence is required.
Finish with individual and team feedback.
coachingPoints: Assess whether running actions solve a football problem.
Record the timing and purpose of support runs.
Observe whether players maintain structure under fatigue.
Assess pressing, recovery and reset behaviours.
Include skill execution in every station.
Monitor transition reaction after turnovers.
Evaluate tactical pacing and scenario understanding.
Modify standards according to role, age and conditioning history.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players create and use outnumbers.
Whether corridor support is timed correctly.
Whether defensive pressing remains connected.
Whether forward structure survives repeated entries.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.
Whether players adjust effort to tactical scenarios.
Whether recovery prepares the next task.
Whether communication remains consistent.

commonErrors.error: Players treat every station as a running test.
commonErrors.correction: Re-emphasise the football objective and tactical role.

commonErrors.error: Support runs occur without creating an option.
commonErrors.correction: Score only movements that influence possession or defence.

commonErrors.error: Team structure collapses under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce station duration or increase recovery.

commonErrors.error: Coaches overlook skill execution.
commonErrors.correction: Record disposal, marking and ground-ball quality separately.

commonErrors.error: Players use maximal intensity in low-risk scenarios.
commonErrors.correction: Assess whether effort matches tactical need.

commonErrors.error: Feedback is based only on work rate.
commonErrors.correction: Include decision making, positioning and recovery in the final review.

progressions: Add full live opposition at every station.
Reduce rotation recovery.
Use role-specific conditioning benchmarks.
Record running and skill metrics where technology is available.
Repeat the assessment after a four-to-six-week advanced conditioning block.
successIndicators: Execute clean football skills under workload.
Adjust physical output to tactical need.
Demonstrate a clear advanced football-conditioning profile.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether conditioning transfers into effective Australian football actions, including creating outnumbers, surging through the corridor, pressing and resetting, repeating forward-entry efforts, reacting to turnovers and managing tactical scenarios.

title: Inside-to-Outside Transition Runs
primarySkill: Repeated transition running from central congestion to outside support
objective: Develop the ability to work from a central possession contest, accelerate into outside space and remain connected when the football transitions between inside and outside lanes.
groundSize: A 60-metre by 50-metre area divided into one central channel and two outside channels.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central channel approximately 20 metres wide.
Mark an outside channel along each side of the area.
Organise groups of four attackers and two controlled defenders.
Begin two attackers inside the central channel and one attacker in each outside channel.
Position one target player beyond the far end.
Place a recovery lane outside the active playing area.
Use 40-second work periods followed by 60 seconds of active recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The football begins with two attackers inside the central channel.
The defenders apply controlled pressure and attempt to close the direct forward route.
One outside player accelerates into space and receives a handball or short kick.
The opposite outside player runs forward to provide the next width option.
The original inside players follow possession and provide central support.
The group moves the football to the target at the far end.
On the coach’s turnover call, all attackers fold back through the central channel.
The defenders receive a new football and attempt to exit through either starting gate.
The original attackers apply recovery pressure until the exit is completed.
Players walk through the outside recovery lane before rotating roles.
Complete four to six work periods.
coachingPoints: Hold outside width until the central possession is controlled.
Accelerate into space rather than waiting stationary.
Use the outside player before the defence can shift.
Follow the football with inside support.
Keep both outside channels available.
React immediately when the turnover is called.
Recover through the corridor before widening defensively.
Preserve disposal quality during repeated transitions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether outside players maintain width before receiving.
Whether the first outside run is timed effectively.
Whether inside players continue supporting after disposal.
Whether turnover recovery begins immediately.
Whether players protect central space during the defensive phase.
Whether skill quality remains stable throughout the work period.

commonErrors.error: Outside players move inside too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the outside channel until the central ball carrier can release.

commonErrors.error: Inside players watch after disposing.
commonErrors.correction: Follow possession and provide the next central option.

commonErrors.error: All attackers use the same outside channel.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a player on each side of the area.

commonErrors.error: Recovery runs go directly towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through the corridor and protect the dangerous space first.

commonErrors.error: Disposal becomes rushed after repeated transitions.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest clean option and maintain balance before release.

progressions: Add another defender.
Allow defenders to create live turnovers.
Reduce the width of the outside channels.
Add a second attacking phase after the first target receives.
Reduce recovery between work periods.
regressions: Predetermine the outside channel to be used.
Use handball only through the central section.
successIndicators: Move the football cleanly between channels.
matchApplication: Teams regularly win possession in congestion and release to outside runners. When possession is lost, those same players must fold back through the centre and protect dangerous space.

title: Defensive-50 Lock-In Conditioning
objective: Develop the ability to repeatedly press a defensive exit, retain the football inside attacking 50 and reorganise for another forward entry.
groundSize: Inside 50 or a 55-metre by 50-metre area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise six to eight forwards against five to seven defenders.
Mark two exit gates near the boundary sides of the defensive area.
Position a coach or midfielder outside 50 with several footballs.
Allocate forward players to pressure, intercept and cover positions.
Use 60-second live periods followed by 90 seconds of active recovery.
Rotate one or two players after every period.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach kicks the football into the forward area.
The attacking group attempts to score.
If the defenders gain possession, they attempt to exit through either gate.
The forwards apply coordinated pressure to prevent the exit.
If the forwards force a turnover or intercept, they immediately attack goal again.
The coach may introduce another football if the first leaves the area quickly.
Play remains live for 60 seconds regardless of scores.
The forwards receive one point for every retained forward entry and two points for a score after a forced turnover.
Defenders receive one point for a clean exit.
Players walk, recover and reorganise for 90 seconds.
Complete four to six periods.
coachingPoints: Pressure the ball carrier while protecting the nearest exit.
Keep one player behind the immediate contest.
Avoid every forward collapsing to the football.
Close space with speed and arrive under control.
Communicate pressure, cover and intercept roles.
React immediately when the football changes possession.
Spread quickly after regaining the football.
Maintain forward structure across repeated entries.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether forward pressure is coordinated.
Whether defenders are forced towards lower-value exits.
Whether intercept players hold useful positions.
Whether forwards react immediately after regaining possession.
Whether the group can reorganise after each scoring attempt.
Whether fatigue causes players to chase individually.

commonErrors.error: Every forward attacks the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain pressure, cover and intercept roles.

commonErrors.error: Boundary exits are left unguarded.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the nearest exit gate before collapsing further inside.

commonErrors.error: Players overrun the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Use short final steps and corral before attempting contact.

commonErrors.error: Forwards remain narrow after regaining possession.
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately to create separate scoring options.

commonErrors.error: Later periods become unstructured chasing.
commonErrors.correction: Pause during recovery and reset role responsibilities.

progressions: Increase the number of defenders.
Reduce the size of the forward area.
Require defenders to complete two possessions before exiting.
Add scoreboard consequences for consecutive defensive exits.
Reduce recovery to 60 seconds.
successIndicators: Force rushed or wide defensive disposals.
Repeat pressure periods without losing team structure.
matchApplication: Sustained forward pressure requires repeated high-intensity efforts, disciplined spacing and immediate attacking reaction when possession is regained.
relatedDrills: CF-053 – Press, Turnover and Counter Run

title: Midfield Spread-and-Fold Waves
primarySkill: Repeated midfield spread and defensive folding
objective: Develop the ability of midfield players to spread rapidly after possession is won and fold defensively when the football is lost.
groundSize: A 60-metre by 50-metre midfield area divided into central, inside-support and outside-support lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central contest zone approximately 15 metres square.
Mark two inside-support lanes and two outside-support lanes.
Organise teams of four or five.
Position one feeder near the central zone.
Place scoring gates at both ends.
Use 35–45-second work periods with 60–75 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder releases a ground ball into the central contest zone.
Both teams compete or apply controlled pressure to win possession.
The team that gains possession spreads immediately into the support lanes.
The ball winner uses a handball or short kick to an inside-support runner.
Outside runners accelerate forward to provide width.
The team attempts to score through the gate at the attacking end.
On a turnover, the former attacking team folds through the central lane.
The new attacking team spreads in the opposite direction.
Play continues for the full work period.
Players walk and reset during recovery.
Complete five to seven periods.
coachingPoints: Spread only after possession is clearly won.
Use different inside and outside running lanes.
Accelerate beyond the ball winner.
Keep one player behind possession for turnover protection.
Fold through central space after losing the football.
Communicate who attacks, supports and covers.
Complete simple disposals at high speed.
Maintain role discipline as fatigue increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether spread occurs immediately after possession is gained.
Whether support runners use separate lanes.
Whether one player remains in a protective position.
Whether players recognise the turnover quickly.
Whether the defensive fold protects the corridor.
Whether disposal quality survives repeated changes of direction.

commonErrors.error: Players spread before possession is secured.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the defensive shape until the football is clearly controlled.

commonErrors.error: All support runners move outside.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain at least one inside-support runner.

commonErrors.error: No player protects behind possession.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate a defensive balance role before each repetition.

commonErrors.error: Players chase the turnover football from the wrong side.
commonErrors.correction: Fold through the corridor and recover goal side.

commonErrors.error: Skill becomes rushed at high speed.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest clean support option and release earlier.

progressions: Add one extra player to each team.
Increase contact to match-like levels for appropriate senior groups.
Reduce the width of the support lanes.
Introduce scoreboard scenarios.
Reduce recovery between periods.
successIndicators: Spread immediately after possession is won.
Repeat high-speed transitions with clean skill.
matchApplication: Midfield groups repeatedly move from congestion into attacking spread and then fold back defensively when possession changes. This drill conditions that complete midfield movement cycle.

title: Forward Press Repeat Entry
primarySkill: Repeated forward pressure followed by renewed forward entry
objective: Develop the ability to pressure a defensive exit, regain possession and immediately reorganise for another purposeful forward entry.
groundSize: From approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise an attacking group of seven to nine and a defending group of six to eight.
Position two midfield feeders outside the forward area.
Place two defensive exit gates near the boundary sides.
Allocate forward roles including high forward, deep target, crumber, pressure players and intercept players.
Use 75-second live periods followed by 90 seconds recovery.
howTheDrillWorks:
A midfielder begins the first forward entry.
The forwards lead, contest and attempt to score.
If defenders gain possession, they attempt to exit through either gate.
The forwards pressure the exit.
If the forwards regain possession, they must release back to a midfielder outside the area.
The midfield group immediately delivers a second forward entry.
Forward players reset their spacing while the football travels outside.
Play continues through repeated entries for 75 seconds.
Attackers score one point for retaining the football inside 50 and two points for a goal after a repeat entry.
Defenders score one point for a clean exit.
Walk, recover and rotate roles.
Complete four to six periods.
coachingPoints: Complete purposeful forward leads rather than all running towards the football.
React immediately when the defenders gain possession.
Pressure the nearest exit while retaining intercept shape.
Release outside after regaining possession to create a fresh entry.
Reset forward spacing quickly.
Crumbers must reposition for each new entry.
Communicate the next leading pattern.
Preserve finishing technique under fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether forward structure exists before each entry.
Whether pressure begins immediately after possession is lost.
Whether intercept positions are retained.
Whether forwards reset after the football is released outside.
Whether the second and third entries have the same movement quality as the first.
Whether decision making remains controlled under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Forwards remain clustered after the first entry.
commonErrors.correction: Release outside and reset players into defined starting lanes.

commonErrors.error: Every forward chases the defensive ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate pressure, cover and intercept responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: The second entry is rushed before structure resets.
commonErrors.correction: Require the midfielder to scan and wait for separated leads.

commonErrors.error: Crumbers stand beneath the aerial contest.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive into the drop zone as the kick approaches.

commonErrors.error: Finishing becomes careless late in the period.
commonErrors.correction: Balance before disposal and reduce live-period length if required.

progressions: Add another defender.
Remove the compulsory release outside after a turnover win.
Limit the time available for each repeat entry.
Add scoreboard pressure.
Reduce recovery to 60 seconds.
successIndicators: Apply immediate pressure after losing possession.
Regain or retain the football inside attacking 50.
Finish accurately during repeated attacking phases.
matchApplication: Teams often create scores through repeat forward entries rather than the initial kick. This drill develops the work rate required to pressure an exit, regain possession and attack again.
relatedDrills: CF-053 – Press, Turnover and Counter Run

title: Backline Exit-to-Recover Chain
primarySkill: Repeated defensive exit followed by recovery to structure
objective: Develop the ability to exit defensive 50 through connected running and then recover rapidly when the rebound possession breaks down.
groundSize: Defensive 50 extending approximately 30 metres beyond the arc.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Organise five to seven defenders and three to five controlled forwards.
Mark two short outlet gates and two longer exit gates.
Place a target player beyond defensive 50.
Position a coach with extra footballs near the attacking side.
Use 45-second work periods followed by 75 seconds recovery.
Allocate defenders to deep, central, outside and overlap roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with a kick or ground ball inside defensive 50.
The defenders secure possession.
The group uses short support and outside width to exit through a gate.
At least one defender must run past possession to create an overlap.
The group attempts to complete a final kick to the target beyond defensive 50.
The coach then calls turnover and introduces a new football towards goal.
All defenders recover to protect the corridor and dangerous forward space.
The forwards attempt to score before the defence resets.
The repetition ends when the defence regains possession, the forwards score or the work period expires.
Players walk and reset during recovery.
Complete five to seven periods.
coachingPoints: Secure the football before spreading.
Create inside and outside exit options.
Run past possession to create rebound momentum.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
React immediately to the turnover call.
Recover through the corridor first.
Communicate deep and high defensive roles.
Re-establish structure rather than chasing every opponent.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders spread after possession is secured.
Whether overlap running creates forward movement.
Whether the final exit kick is controlled.
Whether players react immediately to the turnover.
Whether recovery lines protect the corridor.
Whether the backline communicates during the reset.

commonErrors.error: Defenders spread before possession is secured.
commonErrors.correction: Control the football first and then release into space.

commonErrors.error: No player runs beyond the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate an overlap role before the repetition.

commonErrors.error: Exit kicks are played to stationary targets.
commonErrors.correction: Require receivers to lead into the gate.

commonErrors.error: Players chase the turnover football from behind.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through central space and regain goal-side position.

commonErrors.error: Defenders all collapse deep.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one higher player to protect the next possession.

progressions: Add another forward.
Allow live turnovers rather than a coach call.
Reduce the number of exit gates.
Require two separate defensive exits within one work period.
Reduce recovery between periods.
regressions: Remove forward pressure during the exit.
Pause briefly before the turnover phase.
successIndicators: Re-establish defensive structure before a score occurs.
matchApplication: Defenders must contribute to rebound running without becoming disconnected when possession is lost. This drill conditions the complete exit-and-recovery cycle.

title: High-Speed Ball Movement Endurance
objective: Develop the ability to sustain fast, connected football movement for extended periods without losing disposal quality or team shape.
groundSize: Approximately two-thirds of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the area into defensive, midfield and attacking thirds.
Organise two teams with one neutral support player.
Place two scoring gates at each end.
Mark outside recovery zones along both boundaries.
Use three-minute playing blocks with 90 seconds active recovery.
Begin with controlled defensive pressure and increase over later blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins with possession in the defensive third.
The team attempts to move through all three thirds and score through an end gate.
Players must move after every disposal.
A possession cannot remain in one third for more than eight seconds.
After a score, the opposite team immediately attacks in the other direction.
On turnover, both teams transition without stopping.
Players may use the outside recovery zones only after completing a high-speed support run.
Play continues for three minutes.
Teams walk, recover and discuss spacing for 90 seconds.
Complete four or five blocks.
Increase pressure or reduce time limits only if skill quality remains acceptable.
coachingPoints: Move the football quickly without rushing technique.
Run before the disposal is released.
Use both sides of the ground.
Accelerate to create separation, then control speed before receiving.
Continue supporting after possession enters the next third.
Maintain one player behind the football.
React immediately to turnovers.
Use recovery periods actively.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain movement after disposal.
Whether possession progresses through each third.
Whether both outside lanes are used.
Whether skill remains accurate at speed.
Whether players preserve defensive balance.
Whether repeated three-minute blocks retain the same structure.

commonErrors.error: Players sprint without creating a receiving option.
commonErrors.correction: Run to a visible passing lane rather than merely increasing speed.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement becomes rushed and inaccurate.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the carrier’s final steps and release to the nearest clean option.

commonErrors.error: All players move ahead of possession.
commonErrors.correction: Retain one or two players behind the football.

commonErrors.error: Possession becomes trapped on one side.
commonErrors.correction: Switch through the neutral player or central support.

commonErrors.error: Later blocks lose intensity and shape.
commonErrors.correction: Increase recovery or reduce block length.

progressions: Remove the neutral support player.
Reduce the eight-second zone limit.
Increase defensive pressure.
Add a second football for a controlled short period.
Reduce active recovery to 60 seconds.
successIndicators: Repeat the required standard across all blocks.
matchApplication: High-level Australian football requires teams to move the football at speed for extended periods while maintaining structure, skill and transition readiness.

title: Late-Game Repeat Contest Scenario
primarySkill: Repeat contested efforts under late-game fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to complete repeated contested efforts and make appropriate decisions during a simulated late-game period.
groundSize: A 60-metre by 50-metre area with scoring zones at both ends.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two even teams.
Prepare late-game scenarios including:
Scores level with two minutes remaining.
One team four points ahead.
One team five points behind.
A stoppage inside attacking 50.
A boundary stoppage near defensive 50.
Begin each scenario with a ball-up, boundary throw-in simulation or loose football.
Use 90–120-second scenarios followed by 90 seconds active recovery.
Apply controlled match-like contact appropriate to the group.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, time and field position.
Players organise before the football is released.
The scenario begins with a contested possession.
Teams attempt to score or protect the lead according to the situation.
If the football becomes dead, the coach immediately creates another stoppage nearby.
Players may complete several repeat contests within the same scenario.
The clock continues throughout the scenario.
The scenario ends when time expires or a decisive score occurs.
Players walk, recover and review for 90 seconds.
Swap roles or change the scoreboard situation.
Complete five to seven scenarios.
coachingPoints: Understand the score and time before the contest.
Enter each stoppage with a clear role.
Repeat effort after the first tackle, block or ground-ball action.
Protect dangerous central space when defending a lead.
Use forward movement and urgency when behind.
Maintain legal contact under fatigue.
Communicate the remaining time.
Recover quickly between consecutive stoppages.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the tactical objective.
Whether repeat contest efforts continue after the first action.
Whether stoppage roles remain organised.
Whether decisions match the score and time.
Whether contact remains legal.
Whether fatigue causes players to lose awareness.

commonErrors.error: Players attack every scenario in the same way.
commonErrors.correction: Clarify whether the team must score, retain or defend.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the first contest action.
commonErrors.correction: Score repeat involvement and second efforts.

commonErrors.error: Team ahead takes unnecessary risks.
commonErrors.correction: Use possession and protect dangerous central space.

commonErrors.error: Team behind moves the football too slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Play on and provide immediate forward support.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes uncontrolled late in the scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce contact level or shorten the scenario.

progressions: Remove coach reminders after play begins.
Link two scenarios without full recovery.
Add interchange restrictions.
Use uneven player numbers.
Add wet-weather football handling constraints where conditions are safe.
successIndicators: Preserve work rate and composure late in the scenario.
matchApplication: Late in matches, players must repeatedly contest the football while managing fatigue, score, time and field position. This drill conditions both the physical and tactical demands of those moments.

title: Full-Ground Interchange Rotation Conditioning
primarySkill: Managing repeated match running through interchange rotations
objective: Develop the ability to complete high-intensity football periods, recover through the interchange and re-enter play in a useful positional role.
groundSize: Full oval or a minimum area of 120 metres by 75 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise two teams with two to four interchange players each.
Mark an interchange area along one boundary.
Allocate positional roles to every player.
Use four- or five-minute playing blocks.
Rotate players at 45–90-second intervals.
Prepare re-entry instructions covering wing, midfield, forward and defensive roles.
Use controlled match rules and normal scoring.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins as a normal directional game.
The coach calls one or two players to interchange.
Exiting players leave through the marked area and begin active recovery.
Resting players watch the game and identify team shape.
The coach assigns a re-entry role and gate.
Players re-enter at the next permitted moment.
The first action after re-entry must support possession, pressure or defensive structure.
Rotations continue throughout the playing block.
At the end of the block, all players walk and recover for two minutes.
Coaches review workload, positional balance and successful re-entry actions.
Complete four to six blocks.
coachingPoints: Exit and enter only through the interchange area.
Recover actively rather than sitting immediately.
Remain mentally connected while off the ground.
Identify the team’s current shape before re-entry.
Enter into a specific role, not simply the nearest space.
Communicate with the player being replaced.
Use the first involvement cleanly.
Adjust rotation duration for position, age and training status.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players leave and enter correctly.
Whether recovery is active and controlled.
Whether interchange players remain engaged with play.
Whether re-entry improves team shape.
Whether the first involvement is purposeful.
Whether workload is distributed appropriately.

commonErrors.error: Players switch off while resting.
commonErrors.correction: Require them to identify the next likely role and game phase.

commonErrors.error: Re-entry occurs into congested space.
commonErrors.correction: Scan first and use the assigned positional gate.

commonErrors.error: Players sprint immediately after leaving the field.
commonErrors.correction: Begin recovery with controlled walking and breathing.

commonErrors.error: Rotations leave the team structurally unbalanced.
commonErrors.correction: Replace players by role or adjust another position simultaneously.

commonErrors.error: First disposal after re-entry is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Settle into the role and use the nearest clean option.

progressions: Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Shorten interchange recovery periods.
Restrict the number of available rotations.
Allow player leaders to manage rotations.
Use GPS targets where technology is available.
regressions: Use two broad role groups rather than detailed positions.
successIndicators: Maintain team structure across multiple rotations.
matchApplication: Effective interchange management requires players to recover physically while remaining tactically aware, then return to the ground ready to contribute immediately.

title: Match-Intensity Conditioning Simulation
objective: Develop the ability to sustain match-intensity running, skill, decision making and team structure across extended football periods.
groundSize: Full oval or approximately three-quarters of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Organise two balanced teams with positional structure.
Use normal scoring.
Prepare four phase constraints:
Open match play.
Forward-half pressure.
Defensive rebound.
Late-game scoreboard scenario.
Use six- to eight-minute playing blocks.
Allow two to three minutes active recovery between blocks.
Establish contact and safety rules before beginning.
Prepare interchange rotations where numbers permit.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first block begins with open match play.
Coaches observe work rate, ball movement, defensive recovery and skill quality.
The second block begins with repeated forward entries to one team.
The third block begins from defensive rebound situations.
The final block uses a scoreboard and time scenario.
Play remains continuous within each block.
Coaches minimise stoppages and provide feedback during recovery periods.
Players rotate positions or interchange roles between blocks.
Teams walk, hydrate and review during recovery.
Complete four or five blocks.
End the activity if movement or contact safety falls below the required standard.
coachingPoints: Run with football purpose rather than chasing total distance.
Maintain team structure during extended play.
Repeat efforts after contests and turnovers.
Adjust pace according to the phase.
Execute simple skills under fatigue.
Recover defensively through dangerous central space.
Continue supporting after disposal.
Use recovery periods to prepare for the next block.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether work rate remains purposeful.
Whether players repeat effort after initial contests.
Whether team offence and defence remain connected.
Whether transition reaction changes under fatigue.
Whether skill and decision quality decline.
Whether interchange and recovery habits are effective.
Whether contact remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Players chase running volume without maintaining position.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce role-specific movement and team shape.

commonErrors.error: Intensity is maximal during every phase.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust pace to possession, field position and tactical need.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after disposal or contest.
commonErrors.correction: Score repeat involvement and support running.

commonErrors.error: Skill becomes unnecessarily ambitious under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest clean option and maintain possession.

commonErrors.error: Recovery periods become inactive.
commonErrors.correction: Walk, hydrate, breathe and discuss the next phase.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes unsafe late in blocks.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce contact, shorten blocks or end the activity.

progressions: Increase block duration.
Reduce recovery between blocks.
Add interchange restrictions.
Use full match-like contact for appropriately prepared senior players.
Record GPS, heart-rate, skill and scoring data.
regressions: Run one tactical phase at a time.
successIndicators: Adjust pace to the tactical situation.
matchApplication: This simulation reproduces the combined physical, technical and tactical demands of extended match play rather than isolating fitness from football performance.

title: Conditioning with Football Chapter Final Assessment
objective: Assess whether players can apply the complete physical, technical, tactical and recovery behaviours developed throughout the Conditioning with Football chapter.
groundSize: Full oval or approximately three-quarters of an oval with separate assessment zones.
equipment: Tackle bags or bump pads where required
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Create six assessment components:
Movement Preparation and Mechanics
Progressive football warm-up, acceleration, deceleration and change of direction.
Continuous Football Work
Aerobic possession and high-speed ball movement.
Repeat-Effort and Skill
Repeated running efforts followed by kicking, handballing or ground-ball execution.
Pressure and Contest
Chasing, tackling, ground-ball and aerial-to-ground repeat efforts.
Team Transition
Spread, fold, defensive recovery and attacking support.
Match-Intensity Simulation
Extended football block with scoreboard and interchange conditions.
Divide players into balanced or positional groups.
Allocate five to six minutes to Components 1–5.
Allow 60–90 seconds for rotation.
Finish with an eight- to ten-minute Match-Intensity Simulation.
Prepare assessment categories covering movement quality, work-rate consistency, football skill, decision making, team role, recovery behaviour and safety.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players complete the movement-preparation component at progressively increasing intensity.
Coaches assess acceleration, braking, balance and football movement mechanics.
Groups rotate to continuous football work and sustain possession movement.
Players complete repeat-effort running followed by football execution.
At the pressure and contest component, players demonstrate safe repeat actions.
The team-transition component requires players to spread after possession and fold after turnover.
Players walk during every station rotation.
Coaches record individual and group performance.
After Components 1–5, players complete three minutes of active recovery.
The Match-Intensity Simulation begins with normal play.
Coaches introduce a turnover phase, forward-pressure phase and late-game scenario.
Interchange rotations are managed during the simulation.
The assessment ends with active recovery and a structured review.
Each player receives one identified strength and one specific conditioning-development priority.
coachingPoints: Assess football performance rather than running volume alone.
Record whether movement remains safe and efficient.
Compare first and final efforts for consistency.
Include disposal, marking and ground-ball quality.
Observe decision making under fatigue.
Assess repeated pressure and contest actions.
Record transition reaction after turnovers.
Assess whether players maintain positional and team structure.
Include active recovery and re-entry habits.
Apply age, role, training-history and return-to-play adjustments.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Progressive preparation and movement readiness.
Acceleration and deceleration mechanics.
Sustainable aerobic football movement.
Repeat-effort consistency.
Skill execution before and after fatigue.
Safe contact and contested technique.
Immediate turnover reaction.
Inside and outside support movement.
Defensive recovery and attacking spread.
Communication throughout work and recovery.
Tactical pacing during match simulation.
Whether individual workload remains appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Assessment focuses only on running speed or distance.
commonErrors.correction: Score physical, technical, tactical and recovery behaviours separately.

commonErrors.error: Players begin every component at maximal intensity.
commonErrors.correction: Explain the required workload and purpose before each station.

commonErrors.error: Skill errors are ignored when effort is high.
commonErrors.correction: Make football execution a compulsory assessment category.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes unsafe contact or movement.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce intensity, modify the task or remove the player from that component.

commonErrors.error: All positions are judged against identical running demands.
commonErrors.correction: Apply role-specific expectations and benchmarks.

commonErrors.error: Players stop completely during rotations.
commonErrors.correction: Require walking recovery and early preparation for the next task.

commonErrors.error: Coaches provide broad feedback only.
commonErrors.correction: Identify one observable strength and one specific improvement action.

progressions: Use GPS, heart-rate and skill-efficiency data.
Apply full position-specific performance benchmarks.
Increase live opposition during technical components.
Reduce recovery between components.
Repeat the assessment after a four-to-eight-week conditioning phase.
Compare results across preseason, in-season and return-to-play periods.
regressions: Complete four assessment components rather than six.
Replace live contact with bags or shadow pressure.
Create separate modified, junior, Over 35 and return-to-play groups.
Use individual technical assessment rather than competitive scoring.
successIndicators: Accelerate, decelerate and change direction with control.
Compete at ground and aerial level.
Adjust physical output to tactical needs.
matchApplication: The final assessment combines the complete conditioning demands of Australian football: preparation, sustained movement, acceleration, braking, repeated efforts, contested work, skill under fatigue, transition, tactical pacing, interchange recovery and extended match-intensity performance.
relatedDrills: CF-060 – Pressure and Contest Block Assessment
